tour.description: These are the building blocks the VectorDB façade composes. `distance.rs` is the scalar reference for Euclidean / cosine / dot; `simd_intrinsics.rs` is the same math vectorised across AVX2, AVX2-FMA, AVX-512 and NEON. `index.rs` declares the VectorIndex trait, and `hnsw.rs` is the production implementation — a Hierarchical Navigable Small World graph giving logarithmic-time ANN search with persistence. `storage.rs` is the crash-safe append-only on-disk format. `quantization.rs` provides Scalar/Int8, Product, Int4, and Binary quantized vectors with SIMD-accelerated distances. `embeddings.rs` is the EmbeddingProvider abstraction (local deterministic hash embedder + HTTP API embedder for OpenAI/Cohere).
tour.languageLesson: Rust SIMD is usually written behind `#[cfg(target_feature = …)]` guards plus runtime CPU detection: you compile every kernel (scalar, AVX2, AVX-512, NEON) into the binary and dispatch at runtime via `is_x86_feature_detected!`. That's how a single installed binary can light up AVX-512 on a Sapphire Rapids box and NEON on an M-series Mac without recompilation.

tour.title: The Advanced Features That Make This Not a Toy
tour.description: The differentiators advertised in Step 1 live here. `advanced_features.rs` is the module root. `diskann.rs` is a DiskANN/Vamana graph index for billion-scale on-disk ANN. `hybrid_search.rs` fuses BM25 keyword scores with vector similarity using configurable score normalization. `graph_rag.rs` is the GraphRAG pipeline (entity/relation extraction, community detection, local/global/hybrid retrieval). `matryoshka.rs` is multi-resolution embedding search that funnels from short to full-dim. After install, every one of these is reachable through the CLI verbs in Step 5 and the MCP tool calls in Step 7.

tour.title: Verification Surface — Did the Install Actually Work?
tour.description: Closing the loop on the slice's stated purpose: how do you check the install? `cli_tests.rs` is the assert_cmd-driven smoke suite that exercises `--version`, `--help`, create, info, insert-from-json, search, and benchmark — exactly the commands you'd run by hand. `mcp_tests.rs` validates the JSON-RPC wire format of the embedded MCP server from Step 7. `integration_tests.rs` is the end-to-end VectorDB workflow (insert/search round-trips, 10k-vector batches, persistence reload). `hnsw_search.rs` is the Criterion benchmark you can run to confirm the SIMD kernels from Step 10 are firing on your CPU. Together they constitute the verification surface for `cargo install ruvector-cli`.

tour.title: Orient: What the Brain Is
tour.description: Start with the project- and crate-level READMEs to understand the slice-2 mission. CLAUDE.md frames the pi.ruv.io shared brain as Claude Code's collective memory (1,500+ memories, 350K+ graph edges) with brain_search/brain_share/brain_status tools, while the two crate READMEs split the world into a stdio client (mcp-brain) and a Cloud Run backend (mcp-brain-server) reachable over HTTPS. CHANGELOG.md anchors when the integration landed (the 2.0.4/2.0.5 ruvector-mcp releases). Read these before touching any Rust so the rest of the tour has a story to attach to.

tour.title: Client Entry: The Stdio MCP Server
tour.description: mcp-brain is the client half of the system: it runs locally as a stdio MCP server that Claude Code spawns, and it advertises the brain_* tools. main.rs initializes tracing and hands control to the stdio loop; lib.rs wires up the client/embed/pipeline/server/tools/types modules and re-exports McpBrainServer as the public surface, documenting the ten brain_* MCP tools the crate provides; Cargo.toml pins rmcp, reqwest, and ed25519-dalek so this crate can speak MCP, do HTTPS, and sign witness records.
tour.languageLesson: Rust binaries declared in a workspace come in pairs: src/main.rs is the bin entry (only #[tokio::main] async fn main lives here) and src/lib.rs is the library that the bin AND tests import. Splitting them this way means McpBrainServer can be instantiated from integration tests without booting the stdio loop.

tour.title: Tool Dispatch: How brain_* Calls Are Routed
tour.description: server.rs implements the JSON-RPC stdio protocol (initialize / tools/list / tools/call) and dispatches every call into McpBrainTools, defined in tools.rs. tools.rs is the canonical list of brain tools the client exposes (share, search, vote, transfer, drift, partition, list, delete, status, sync, plus page/node lifecycle) and translates each call into an HTTP request against the cloud backend. types.rs catalogs the BrainMemory, category, drift-response, and JSON-RPC envelope shapes that ride the wire. This is the layer Claude Code actually talks to.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's enum + Result combo is what makes MCP dispatch tractable. BrainError variants in tools.rs implement std::error::Error and are returned as Result<Value, BrainError>; the server.rs layer pattern-matches and converts to JSON-RPC error responses without any try/catch ceremony.

tour.title: Client to Cloud Bridge: HTTP + Embeddings + Witness
tour.description: When a Claude Code session calls brain_search, the client embeds the query locally and POSTs it to pi.ruv.io. client.rs is the reqwest-based BrainClient that holds the API key and exposes typed methods for every cloud REST endpoint. embed.rs produces 128-dim vectors via multi-granularity SHAKE-256 hashing plus a rank-2 MicroLoRA federated transform — that's why brain_search works offline-ish without bundling a heavy model. pipeline.rs strips PII via regex and builds the rolling SHA-3 witness chain that the server verifies before accepting a share.
tour.languageLesson: Witness chains in Rust use a rolling hash: each new entry's hash = H(prev_hash || payload), implemented here on top of sha3::Sha3_256 / Shake256 from the sha3 crate. Tamper-evidence falls out of the data structure — no extra protocol round-trips needed.

tour.title: Server Boot: Axum Router and AppState
tour.description: Crossing the wire, we arrive at the Cloud Run backend. mcp-brain-server's main.rs is intentionally minimal: it builds the axum router, binds PORT immediately (so Cloud Run's startup probe passes), then spawns the cognitive training and tick loops in the background. lib.rs is the crate root that re-exports every submodule (store, embeddings, routes, optimizer, web memory, trainer, etc.) and is the highest fan-out node in the graph (28 outbound edges) — it's the index of the entire backend. Cargo.toml declares the axum/tokio/reqwest/sqlx/sha3/ed25519 dependency graph and the feature flags that toggle subsystems on and off.
tour.languageLesson: Cloud Run grades a service 'ready' as soon as it accepts a TCP connection on $PORT. The pattern here — bind the listener, then tokio::spawn the heavy startup work — is idiomatic for any long-warmup Rust service. If you blocked on training/tick init before binding, the revision would fail startup health checks even though the binary is fine.

tour.title: The REST Surface and Shared Types
tour.description: routes.rs is the canonical Brain REST API — 91+ axum handlers spanning memory share/search/vote, training, drift, partition, LoRA federation, Brainpedia pages, WASM nodes, Pub/Sub ingest, Google Chat, Resend inbound, and internal queue endpoints. Every brain_* MCP tool from Step 3 lands on a handler here. types.rs is the central catalog (~73 structs/enums) including AppState (the shared dependency container threaded through every handler) and the request/response shapes — it has the highest fan-in in the graph (10 inbound edges) for good reason. notify.rs handles the transactional email and open-tracking that fans out from /v1/notify endpoints via Resend.
tour.languageLesson: Axum handlers use extractors: function arguments like State<AppState>, Json<Request>, and custom auth extractors are pulled from the request context by type. This is why types.rs has such high fan-in — adding a new endpoint usually means adding a struct here, deriving Serialize/Deserialize, and writing a single async fn handler(...) -> impl IntoResponse.

tour.title: Ingest Pipeline: Getting Knowledge In
tour.description: Building on the REST surface from Step 6, this layer turns raw inputs into stored memories. pipeline.rs is the master ingest/training pipeline: builds RVF containers, ingests from Pub/Sub + RSS/Atom + CommonCrawl/CDX, dedups, runs the optimization scheduler, and emits metrics. web_ingest.rs is the 7-phase web ingestion pipeline (validate, SHAKE-256 dedup, chunk+embed via ruvLLM, novelty scoring, tier assignment, graph edge construction, proof verification) defined in ADR-094. pubmed.rs runs esearch/efetch against the biomedical literature index and detects emerging topics; pubmed_discover.sh wraps it for cron-style invocation.

tour.title: Storage: Firestore, GCS, Quantization
tour.description: Once a memory survives ingest, it lands in the storage layer. store.rs is the largest backend module — FirestoreClient handles auth, memory CRUD, vote tracking, reputation, page/delta lifecycle, and node publish/revoke. gcs.rs is the Google Cloud Storage client for RVF artifact blobs (OAuth via the metadata server, upload/download by contributor + memory id). web_store.rs persists web-derived memories with content-hash dedup and delta indexes. quantization.rs implements PiQ3 tier-aware product quantization (4-bit ~2.67x at 99% recall, 3-bit ~10.7x at 96%, 2-bit ~16x at 90%) so that hot/warm/archived memories cost different storage tiers — ADR-115.

tour.title: Cognitive & Symbolic Layer
tour.description: Above the store sits the layer that makes the brain more than a vector database. cognitive.rs combines Hopfield associative memory, dentate-gyrus pattern separation, and Hyperdimensional Computing for storing/recalling patterns and detecting anomalies. symbolic.rs is the neural-symbolic bridge — extracts grounded propositions from clusters and applies Horn-clause inference over embedding-similar premises. midstream.rs wires category-attractor analysis, solver-confidence scoring, and strange-loop creation via the MIDSTREAM_* runtime knobs. voice.rs models an InternalVoice loop (observations, questions, hypotheses, reflections) with decaying working memory. graph.rs binds it all to ruvector-mincut/solver/sparsifier for ranked search and spectral analytics.

tour.title: Security & Verification
tour.description: Every write into the brain must survive this gauntlet. auth.rs is an axum extractor that validates the API key header and derives a pseudonym from the system seed (so contributors aren't tracked by raw key). verify.rs enforces size limits, strips PII, checks ed25519 signatures, and validates the witness chain built by the client in Step 4 — the round-trip that proves provenance. rate_limit.rs is a per-contributor and per-IP token-bucket limiter with periodic cleanup. reputation.rs scores contributors using Bayesian accuracy updates, poisoning penalties, and inactivity decay; reputation feeds back into the BFT aggregator in aggregate.rs, which bounds outlier influence when merging brain_share contributions.
tour.languageLesson: ed25519-dalek's SigningKey/VerifyingKey API is intentionally infallible-on-correct-input: verify() returns Result<(), SignatureError> and the only error is 'signature does not match'. Pair this with the witness chain from Step 4 — each entry signs its rolling hash — and you get tamper-evidence that's cheap to check on every brain_share request.

tour.title: Scheduled Optimization Jobs
tour.description: Continuous improvement runs out-of-band from the request path. trainer.rs defines the cross-domain discovery cycle (SpaceScience, EarthScience, AcademicResearch, EconomicsFinance, MedicalGenomics, MaterialsPhysics) and the altruistic-knowledge principles. drift.rs maintains rolling per-domain centroid histories and computes coefficient-of-variation + delta sparsity reports via ruvector-delta-core. The ruvbrain_worker bin (a separate Cloud Run Jobs container) invokes train, drift_check, transfer_all, rebuild_graph, cleanup, and attractor_analysis as one-shot CLI actions. scheduler-jobs.yaml + deploy-scheduler.sh wire the seven Cloud Scheduler jobs (train every 5 min, drift 15 min, transfer 30 min, graph hourly, attractor 20 min, full sweep 3 AM, cleanup 4 AM) to /v1/pipeline/optimize via OIDC-authenticated POSTs.

tour.title: The Coherence Gate (Separate Concern)
tour.description: mcp-gate is a sibling crate to mcp-brain — same MCP server pattern, completely different domain. Its job is the Anytime-Valid Coherence Gate: decide permit / defer / deny on an agent action before it executes, with a receipt that can be replayed. main.rs loads config and serves the gate, lib.rs wraps cognitum_gate_tilezero::TileZero with configurable GateThresholds, server.rs handles MCP initialize/tools/call, tools.rs exposes permit_action / get_receipt / replay_decision plus the witness/structural/predictive/evidential helpers, and types.rs defines the permit/defer/deny response shapes. Cargo.toml declares its dependencies. Keep this layer separate from the brain — they share infrastructure but no business logic.

tour.title: Alternate Binaries: SSE, Local Self-Host, Tests
tour.description: Beyond the main Cloud Run server, the crate ships alternate bins for different deployment modes. ruvbrain_sse.rs wraps the brain with an MCP-over-HTTP SSE transport, exposing /health, /sse, and /messages for streaming agent sessions. bin/local.rs is the self-host build — SQLite persistence, Vamana/brute-force cosine index, inline AIDefence prompt-injection/PII scanning, and a minimal axum API — for users who want the brain without GCP. tests.rs is the integration suite covering ranking, drift detection, cognitive memory, witness verification, auth, and core types. static/index.html and origin.html are the browser dashboards served by the same axum router. .env.example documents every runtime variable the bins read.

tour.title: Cloud Operations: Build and Ship
tour.description: Closing the loop on how this gets to production. Five Dockerfiles split the build matrix: Dockerfile (main axum REST image, Rust nightly-2026-03-20 → slim Debian), Dockerfile.sse (SSE transport variant), Dockerfile.worker (background ingestion/training jobs), Dockerfile.trainer (daily discovery binary), Dockerfile.minimal (pre-built binary into slim Debian). Four cloudbuild-*.yaml files are the matching Cloud Build pipelines that produce each image on E2_HIGHCPU machines. deploy.sh is the master orchestrator supporting Path A (dev: direct Cloud Run URL) and Path B (prod: external HTTPS LB + Cloud Armor + CDN + brain.ruv.io). Cargo.workspace.toml is the patched workspace manifest the Docker build uses to pin redb/hnsw_rs/simsimd/tokio/rkyv across 17 brain-stack crates.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds for Rust services follow a fixed shape: stage 1 = full rust:nightly image with the Cargo cache, builds the binary; stage 2 = debian-bookworm-slim with just the binary plus runtime libs (libssl, ca-certificates). Final image stays under a few hundred MB even though the build stage pulls gigabytes of crates. The Cargo.workspace.toml patches in this repo are needed because the Docker build context doesn't include the full RuVector workspace tree.

tour.title: Public Surface: Discovery and Agent Onboarding
tour.description: Wrapping the tour with what the outside world sees. brain-manifest.json is served at /.well-known/brain-manifest.json and advertises the brain's capabilities (memory count, embedders, HNSW + spectral-mincut graph, MicroLoRA federation, BFT consensus, rate limits, infrastructure footprint) so agent crawlers can discover them programmatically. agent-guide.md documents how AI agents should call brain_status/search/share/list and respect rate limits. sitemap.xml exposes the public URLs (homepage, /origin, /v1/status, /v1/health). robots.txt controls crawler access. monitoring-dashboard.json is the GCP Cloud Monitoring mosaicLayout tracking request volume, latency, and error rate for the ruvbrain Cloud Run service. Together these are how the brain stays operable and discoverable in production.

tour.title: Slice 3 Orientation: Four Foundational Crates
tour.description: Slice 3 establishes the neural-primitive foundation that downstream RuVector algorithms (attention, mincut, GNN) build on. These four READMEs introduce the responsibilities: ruvector-math (geometric and information-theoretic primitives), ruvector-graph (distributed Neo4j-compatible hypergraph DB), ruvector-dag (DAG structures with attention, SONA, self-healing, post-quantum crypto), and ruvector-cnn (SIMD/INT8 CNN feature extraction). Read them as the table of contents for the tour.

tour.title: Slice 3 Crate Manifests & Public Surface
tour.description: Each crate's Cargo.toml declares its feature flags (SIMD ISAs, INT8, contrastive, distributed, qudag, ...) and dependency graph, while lib.rs is the canonical entry that re-exports the public API. Together they define the compile-time configuration matrix and the runtime symbol surface you will navigate for the rest of the tour.
tour.languageLesson: Rust crates use Cargo features (e.g. `simd-avx2`, `int8`, `distributed`) to gate `#[cfg(feature = "x")]` code paths so a single source tree compiles into many runtime profiles.

tour.title: Slice 3 Math I: Information Geometry & Manifolds
tour.description: Information geometry treats probability distributions as a Riemannian manifold; Fisher information defines the metric tensor, and natural gradients descend along that geometry rather than naive Euclidean directions. These files implement the Fisher matrix, K-FAC approximation, the natural-gradient step, and the product-manifold abstraction that lets later code mix spherical/hyperbolic/Euclidean factors in one operation.
tour.languageLesson: Rust generics with `T: Float` bounds let one Fisher implementation specialize to `f32` (SIMD-friendly) or `f64` (precision) without code duplication.

tour.title: Slice 3 Math II: Optimal Transport, Spectral & Persistent Homology
tour.description: Optimal transport gives a principled distance between distributions; Sinkhorn entropically regularizes the problem so it becomes a fixed-point iteration on a matrix-scaling, and sliced Wasserstein avoids the quadratic blow-up by 1D projection. Pair these with Chebyshev polynomial filters and persistent homology to get the spectral + topological toolkit consumed by GNN and clustering code later.

tour.title: Slice 3 Math III: Tensor Networks
tour.description: Tensor networks factor high-dimensional arrays into chains/trees of small cores, exposing low-rank structure that dense linear algebra would miss. CP, Tucker, and Tensor-Train decompositions provide three trade-off points (rank vs. flexibility vs. memory) and are the substrate for compressed neural representations used by slice 2 attention/embedding code.

tour.title: Slice 3 Graph: Storage, Transactions & Sharding
tour.description: The hypergraph DB layer mirrors Neo4j's property-graph model but adds true hyperedges (relations on more than two nodes). graph.rs assembles the storage primitives (nodes, hyperedges, transactions) into a coherent store; the distributed/ tree (shard, coordinator) then federates that store horizontally so the same Cypher API addresses a sharded cluster transparently.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's `RwLock` and `Arc` give shared-read/exclusive-write semantics without a GC; transactions wrap the same primitives in a snapshot to give ACID semantics on top of a lock-free read path.

tour.title: Slice 3 Graph: Cypher Pipeline (Parse to JIT to Operators)
tour.description: A Cypher string travels through parser -> semantic analyzer -> optimizer -> physical plan -> JIT-compiled kernel -> physical operators (NodeScan/EdgeScan/Filter/Join/...) before touching storage. Each stage is its own module so you can intercept at any level. ARCHITECTURE.md maps the full pipeline; query_jit.rs is the surprise — hot plans are lowered to executable code for column-stride performance.

tour.title: Slice 3 Graph: Hybrid AI Surface (GNN + RAG + Semantic Search)
tour.description: On top of the operators from Step 7, the hybrid layer composes GNNs, vector indexes, semantic search, and RAG so a single Cypher query can mix graph traversal with vector retrieval. This is the key differentiator versus stock Neo4j and the bridge into the DAG/attention work in later steps.

tour.title: Slice 3 DAG: Core Structures & Mincut Engines
tour.description: QueryDag is the in-memory plan representation that the DAG crate operates on: operator nodes carry kernel metadata, traversal iterators expose topological/DFS/BFS orderings, and the mincut engine partitions the DAG to find optimal cut points (used later by mincut-gated attention). This is the data structure that all subsequent DAG-layer features manipulate.
tour.languageLesson: Rust uses petgraph-style index-based graphs (`NodeIndex`/`EdgeIndex`) instead of pointer-based ones — this side-steps borrow-checker conflicts when an operation needs to read and mutate the graph simultaneously.

tour.title: Slice 3 DAG: Attention Mechanisms
tour.description: The DagAttention trait abstracts multiple attention variants over the DAG: topological (forward-only), causal-cone (history-bounded), hierarchical Lorentz (curved-space across DAG depth), and mincut-gated (uses Step 9's mincut to throttle cross-cluster attention). The IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES doc explains the trade-offs between them — read it first, then skim each variant.
tour.languageLesson: A trait-based attention dispatch (`Box<dyn DagAttention>`) keeps each variant in its own module while letting the executor pick at runtime — the Rust equivalent of a strategy class hierarchy in OO languages.

tour.title: Slice 3 DAG: SONA Continual Learning & Self-Healing
tour.description: SONA (Self-Organizing Neural Architecture) is the cognitive loop: a reasoning bank stores task-conditioned trajectories, EWC++ penalizes weights drifting from prior tasks (preventing catastrophic forgetting), and MicroLoRA injects task-specific low-rank deltas. Paired with it, the healing orchestrator runs anomaly + drift detection and dispatches repair strategies — SONA improves the model, healing keeps the runtime sane.

tour.title: Slice 3 DAG: Post-Quantum QuDAG
tour.description: QuDAG hardens the DAG for a post-quantum future: ML-KEM (lattice-based KEM) for key exchange, ML-DSA (Dilithium) for signatures, identities wrap those primitives, and the network layer carries the resulting authenticated traffic. Tokens/rewards bolt staking on top, making QuDAG a distributed-incentive substrate as well as a crypto layer.

tour.title: Slice 3 CNN: Backbone, Layers & SIMD Kernels
tour.description: ruvector-cnn delivers compact feature extraction. The MobileNetV3 backbone composes layer primitives (Conv2D, batchnorm, linear, pooling) into an efficient inverted-residual stack. The simd/ tree then ships per-ISA implementations of the same kernel — AVX2/AVX-512 for x86, NEON for ARM, WASM SIMD for the browser, plus a scalar reference path and Winograd F(2,3) transforms — dispatched at runtime via CPU feature detection.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's `std::arch` exposes SIMD intrinsics behind `#[target_feature(enable = "avx2")]` and `unsafe fn`. A safe outer wrapper does runtime CPU detection once and then dispatches into the appropriate intrinsic kernel — keeping `unsafe` contained while still going fast. Const generics on layer types let the compiler monomorphize a 3x3 conv into a fully unrolled loop.

tour.title: Slice 3 CNN: INT8 Quantization Pipeline
tour.description: Quantization replaces fp32 weights with int8 plus per-tensor scales and zero-points. params.rs defines the representation; calibration.rs computes scales from a calibration dataset; graph_rewrite.rs lowers the fp32 graph from Step 13 into INT8 ops; int8/kernels/simd.rs is the matching SIMD kernel. tests/kernel_equivalence.rs proves the INT8 path stays within tolerance of fp32.

tour.title: Slice 3 Capstone: Contrastive Training & Exotic Examples
tour.description: The contrastive module (InfoNCE, triplet loss, augmentation) trains the CNN embeddings the rest of RuVector consumes. The exotic examples (synthetic reflex organism, living simulation, self-healing demo) compose every primitive from this tour — math manifolds, hypergraph storage, DAG attention, SONA learning, healing, and CNN features — into runnable scenarios. These are the integration tests for the entire neural-primitive stack and the on-ramp into slices 1 and 2.

tour.title: Slice 4 Orientation: Attention/Mincut Stack
tour.description: Slice 4 is the algorithm layer that sits between slice-3 graph/math primitives and downstream agents. Its central insight is that softmax — the attention bottleneck of modern transformers — can be REPLACED by a dynamic graph min-cut, gated by a hysteresis policy. These three READMEs introduce the three pillars: ruvector-attn-mincut (the fusion seam), ruvector-mincut-gated-transformer (the production transformer that uses the seam), and ruvector-attention (the geometric attention zoo that feeds it).

tour.title: Slice 4 Bridge: The attn-mincut Crate
tour.description: Start at the smallest, most conceptually pure crate: ruvector-attn-mincut. Only nine files — graph_from_logits converts Q·Kᵀ scores into a weighted directed graph, mincut.rs runs Dinic max-flow to discover the cut, gating.rs blends mincut-derived edge masks back into softmax, and hysteresis.rs forces tau consecutive consistent steps before flipping a mask. This is the conceptual fusion point — read it before anything else.
tour.languageLesson: Rust trait dispatch: the attn-mincut crate keeps its surface small by exposing free functions (graph_from_logits, attn_mincut) rather than wide trait hierarchies. When a bridge has one clear job, prefer functions over generics — traits are for polymorphism, not namespacing.

tour.title: Slice 4 Attention: Trait Surface & Crate Root
tour.description: Before the geometric variants, see the contract they all satisfy. traits.rs defines Attention, GraphAttention, GeometricAttention, SparseAttention, TrainableAttention plus shared structs (SparseMask, EdgeInfo, Gradients). lib.rs re-exports the entire ruvector-attention zoo (sheaf, hyperbolic, info-geometry, MoE, PDE, sparse, topology, transport, training, curvature, graph). Together they tell you what 'an attention' MEANS in slice 4: not one algorithm, but a family unified by a trait surface.
tour.languageLesson: Rust associated types let traits speak in terms of 'whatever shape this implementor uses' (e.g. type Output, type Error). Slice-4 attention traits use this pattern so the same trait fits dense f32 tensors and quantized INT8 packed buffers without runtime cost.

tour.title: Slice 4 Attention: Geometric Core
tour.description: The geometric attention family answers 'what KIND of similarity does attention measure?'. Sheaf attention computes Dirichlet energy via per-edge restriction maps (cohomology over a cellular sheaf). Hyperbolic attention replaces Euclidean dot-products with Poincaré-ball distances to encode hierarchies natively. Sliced-Wasserstein uses 1D optimal-transport on random projections for distributional similarity. Mixed-curvature lets different heads live on different manifolds, while PDE-attention models information flow as diffusion.
tour.languageLesson: Rust const generics encode manifold dimensions in the type system: `Poincare<const D: usize>` lets the compiler verify that a 64-dim hyperbolic ball can't be mixed with a 128-dim one. Errors that would be runtime shape mismatches in PyTorch are compile errors here.

tour.title: Slice 4 Attention: Flash, Sparse & Latent KV
tour.description: Where Step 4 was about exotic geometry, this step is about making attention FAST. FlashAttention-3 tiles Q/K/V to keep the working set in cache and uses online softmax (plus Ring Attention for cross-device sharding). Linear attention with kernel feature maps drops cost to O(N). Local+Global sparse attention combines a sliding window with a few global tokens. MLA (DeepSeek-V2/V3 Multi-Head Latent Attention) compresses K/V into a low-rank latent for ~93% KV reduction. ssm.rs is the Mamba SSM non-attention long-range alternative.
tour.languageLesson: Rust SIMD: `std::simd` (portable) and `core::arch::x86_64` (AVX2/AVX-512 intrinsics) let the FlashAttention kernel express tile-wise softmax in vector lanes. Mark hot inner loops `#[inline(always)]` and pin tile sizes with const generics so the autovectorizer can unroll.

tour.title: Slice 4 Attention: Routing, MoE & Topology Gating
tour.description: Attention doesn't just compute — it also DECIDES. MoE router does top-k expert selection with load-balancing loss; moe_attention.rs is the MoE-wrapped attention block. Speculative decoding runs a cheap draft model and validates with the full one. Topology-gated attention is the slice-4 specialty: a coherence signal switches between full / sparse / retrieval-only modes mid-inference, providing the runtime knob that downstream mincut-gating turns.

tour.title: Slice 4 Mincut: Core Algorithm Surface
tour.description: Now flip to the mincut side. ARCHITECTURE.md is the module map; the crate root declares 30 modules. The DynamicGraph in graph/mod.rs is the most-imported file in the slice (fan-in 56) — it is the shared mutable weighted graph backing canonical, dynamic, hierarchy, snn, and optimization modules. canonical/dynamic/mod.rs maintains a min-cut across incremental edge insertions and deletions with periodic full recomputation: this is what gives the attn-mincut bridge its 'dynamic' property.
tour.languageLesson: Rust `&mut` exclusivity: a graph mutated by many algorithms (canonical, snn, optimization) must be borrowed exclusively at each call. The slice-4 mincut crate uses interior mutability (RefCell, Mutex) sparingly and prefers passing `&mut DynamicGraph` because it makes the data dependency explicit at every call site.

tour.title: Slice 4 Mincut: Sparsification & J-Tree
tour.description: The subpolynomial guarantee comes from sparsification. The j-tree (junction tree) is a hierarchical decomposition that lets the dynamic mincut run on a much smaller proxy graph; coordinator.rs orchestrates updates across levels, hierarchy.rs maintains the tree of contracted clusters, sparsifier.rs is the low-recourse Benczur-Karger-style cut sparsifier, and dspar.rs is a degree-based pre-sparsifier. Together these turn a polynomial mincut into something fast enough to call inside an attention head.

tour.title: Slice 4 Mincut: Classical Algorithms & Connectivity
tour.description: The classical mincut machinery that powers the attn-mincut bridge's Dinic call from Step 2. Approximate algorithms (Karger-Stein-style) give probabilistic-correct fast cuts. polylog.rs implements polylogarithmic-time connectivity. localkcut/paper_impl.rs is deterministic local k-cut from the paper. expander/mod.rs is expander decomposition, the structural primitive that makes everything else fast. linkcut/mod.rs is the link-cut tree backing dynamic graph updates.

tour.title: Slice 4 Mincut: SNN Morphogenetic Networks
tour.description: The most exotic mincut feature: a spiking neural network with self-modifying topology. Six layers integrate with dynamic mincut — network.rs is the wiring, attractor.rs and time_crystal.rs are the dynamical regimes, morphogenetic.rs grows new structure under load, and cognitive_engine.rs binds them. The mincut runs continuously to identify weak partitions; the SNN prunes/grows synapses to keep coherence high. This is where mincut becomes a control signal, not just a measurement.

tour.title: Slice 4 Mincut: Runtime, Witness & WASM
tour.description: Algorithms need a runtime. optimization/pool.rs is an arena allocator that keeps mincut hot-path allocations off the global allocator. optimization/parallel.rs is the work-stealing parallel runtime; simd_distance.rs vectorises pair distances. witness/mod.rs is the determinism story: every cut decision emits a signed witness so the audit trail can be replayed. wasm/canonical.rs exposes the same algorithms to browsers and agent runtimes via WASM bindings, so a mincut decision can run in a Cloudflare Worker.
tour.languageLesson: Rust WASM via wasm-bindgen: marking a function `#[wasm_bindgen]` generates a JS shim and serialises arguments through a typed boundary. Slice-4 mincut keeps the WASM surface narrow (canonical.rs, simd.rs, agentic.rs) because every exported function widens the JS attack surface and bloats the .wasm payload.

tour.title: Slice 4 Transformer: Kernels, FlashAttention & Mamba
tour.description: ruvector-mincut-gated-transformer is the production transformer that consumes everything above. THEORY.md explains the coherence-gated math. flash_attention.rs is the FlashAttention-style tiled CPU kernel with online softmax and fused tiled GEMM. mamba.rs is the SSM long-range branch. kernel/qgemm.rs is INT8 matmul. model.rs assembles these into the forward pass.
tour.languageLesson: Rust block-tiled GEMM: const-generic tile sizes (`const TILE_M: usize = 32`) let LLVM unroll the inner three loops completely. Combined with `#[target_feature(enable = "avx2")]` on the hot function, you get hand-tuned assembly without writing it.

tour.title: Slice 4 Transformer: KV Cache Family
tour.description: Modern transformer inference is bottlenecked on KV cache memory bandwidth, not FLOPs. hot_buffer.rs keeps the most recent tokens uncompressed for speed. quantized_store.rs holds older tokens at INT8/INT4. tier.rs orchestrates eviction across hot/warm/cold tiers. kivi.rs implements KIVI 2-bit, kvquant.rs implements KVQuant, squat.rs implements SQuAT. This is what makes long-context inference fit in memory.

tour.title: Slice 4 Transformer: Gate Policies & Tiered Control
tour.description: This is where slice 4's whole thesis lands. gate.rs's GateController fuses energy-gate + config signals into a TierDecision (full / reduced / safe / intervention) — full attention when coherent, sparse when not, retrieval-only when degrading, halt on intervention. energy_gate.rs measures attention energy, sparse_attention.rs is the mincut-derived sparse mask, mod_routing.rs is Mixture-of-Depths token-level routing, and trace.rs tracks lambda-trend so the gate has temporal context.
tour.languageLesson: Rust enum-as-decision: `enum TierDecision { Full, Reduced, Safe, Intervention }` plus exhaustive `match` makes it a compile error to forget a tier when the gate adds a new mode. Encode policy outcomes as enums, not booleans, so the type system enforces coverage.

tour.title: Slice 4 GNN: HNSW + Continual Learning
tour.description: ruvector-gnn is the learning-side companion to the algorithm-side mincut. layer.rs is the GNN message-passing layer running over slice-3's HNSW topology. ewc.rs implements Elastic Weight Consolidation for continual learning without catastrophic forgetting. graphmae.rs is GraphMAE self-supervised pretraining. scheduler.rs detects drift and decides when to retrain. mmap.rs pages features in/out of disk so the GNN can index billions of nodes. The output: embeddings that feed back into the attention/mincut stack.

tour.title: Slice 4 Capstone: Tests, Benches & End-to-End Examples
tour.description: Close the tour by seeing slice 4 run. BENCHMARK_REPORT.md publishes the measured numbers. determinism.rs validates that witness-logged decisions replay bit-identically. paper_algorithms_bench.rs validates the subpolynomial-mincut paper claims. latency.rs benchmarks the gated-transformer hot path. flash_attention_demo.rs is a runnable end-to-end example. This is your starting point for adding a new attention variant or a new mincut algorithm.

tour.title: Slice 5a Orientation: ruvllm in the RuVector Stack
tour.description: Start with the ruvllm crate README to ground yourself in what this slice delivers — a Rust LLM inference engine that sits on top of slices 1-4 (vectors, sparsifiers, mincut, attention primitives) and exposes serving, training, and continual-learning APIs to the rest of RuVector. The CHANGELOG and Cargo.toml round out the picture by showing how the crate's feature flags gate Candle, Mistral.rs, CoreML, Metal, BitNet, and Claude Flow backends behind opt-in builds. Read these before any code so the module names you encounter later map to a published feature surface, not just files on disk.

tour.title: ruvllm Crate Root: RuvLLMEngine Facade
tour.description: lib.rs is the entry point the BFS analysis identified as the top code node — it re-exports every submodule and defines RuvLLMEngine/RuvLLMConfig, the facade that wires sessions, policy store, witness log, and Sona together. error.rs is the single most depended-on file in slice 5a (fan-in 82): nearly every module returns RuvLLMError, so understanding its variants tells you what can go wrong across the stack. types.rs holds the shared GenerateRequest/Response/Token shapes that flow through scheduling, generation, and streaming.
tour.languageLesson: Rust crates use `lib.rs` as the implicit module root. `pub use` re-exports flatten the public API so consumers can write `ruvllm::RuvLLMEngine` instead of `ruvllm::engine::RuvLLMEngine`. The pattern is called a facade or barrel module.

tour.title: Serving Engine: Continuous Batching & Paged KV Cache
tour.description: This is the runtime heart of ruvllm. engine.rs submits, schedules, generates, streams, and times out inference requests; scheduler.rs runs the continuous-batching loop with priority queues, prefill/decode interleaving, preemption, and eviction; kv_cache_manager.rs allocates block-aligned cache slots per request with swap-in/out for long-context tenants; batch.rs plans iterations against a token budget. Together they implement the same paged-attention + continuous-batching design popularized by vLLM, but in Rust and integrated with the rest of RuVector. speculative.rs adds draft/verify decoding with tree-of-thoughts speculation and NEON-optimized sampling on top.

tour.title: Backends: Candle / Mistral.rs / CoreML / Hybrid Dispatch
tour.description: The serving engine doesn't run models directly — it dispatches through the LlmBackend trait defined in backends/mod.rs (the second-most depended-on node after error.rs). candle_backend.rs is the default pure-Rust path using Candle; mistral_backend.rs adds production-grade Mistral.rs with PagedAttention + X-LoRA + in-situ quantization; coreml_backend.rs targets Apple's Neural Engine via .mlpackage. hybrid_pipeline.rs is the most interesting one: it routes each transformer op (flash attention, MLP, RMSNorm, RoPE) to whichever accelerator on Apple Silicon (CPU, Metal, or ANE) wins per-layer, and records per-accelerator timings. autodetect.rs + capabilities.rs decide which backend the engine picks at startup.
tour.languageLesson: Rust traits as compile-time interfaces let you implement `LlmBackend` for radically different runtimes (Candle, Mistral.rs, CoreML) and select between them via a `Box<dyn LlmBackend>`. Feature flags in Cargo.toml conditionally compile each backend so consumers only pay for what they use.

tour.title: Models: RuvLtra Architectures + GGUF Loading
tour.description: ruvltra.rs and ruvltra_medium.rs define the actual decoder-only transformer architectures (Qwen-0.5B/1.8B presets plus a medium GQA variant with RoPE and Sona hooks). They are designed to be loaded from GGUF — the quantization-friendly file format pioneered by llama.cpp. gguf/parser.rs streams headers, metadata, and tensor descriptors; gguf/loader.rs mmaps the file, filters layers, and translates upstream tensor names to ruvllm's internal naming via TensorNameMapper. The ruvltra_small.json descriptor seeds the registry with hardware requirements.

tour.title: Metal GPU: Shaders & Host Pipelines
tour.description: On Apple Silicon, the hybrid pipeline from Step 4 drops into hand-written Metal Shading Language for the hottest kernels. metal/mod.rs declares the kernel parameter structs and device-info gating; pipelines.rs compiles MSL shaders on demand and caches MTLComputePipelineState objects keyed by config; operations.rs / buffers.rs / context.rs wrap dispatch. The .metal files implement Flash Attention 2 with online softmax rescaling against simdgroup_matrix on M-series chips, fused GEMM/GEMV, RoPE, and norm kernels. This is where ruvllm earns its tokens-per-second on Mac.
tour.languageLesson: Metal Shading Language (MSL) is a C++14-based GPU language. `simdgroup_matrix<T, 8, 8>` exposes Apple's tensor-core-equivalent matrix instructions — Flash Attention 2 tiles Q/K/V into these blocks and runs an online softmax rescaling pass to avoid materializing the full N×N attention matrix.

tour.title: Attention Kernels: Flash Attention 2, Paged Attention, RoPE, Norms
tour.description: Cross-platform CPU fallbacks live in kernels/. attention.rs implements Flash Attention v2 with NEON and scalar paths plus multi-query/grouped-query variants; paged_attention.rs (depth-1 in the BFS, fan-in 6) gives the serving layer the non-contiguous KV memory it needs for high concurrency. rope.rs is NEON-accelerated rotary embeddings with NTK-aware scaling for LLaMA-2/3 and Mistral; norm.rs holds the RMSNorm/LayerNorm hot paths every layer hits. activations.rs and matmul.rs round out the kernel surface so non-Apple hardware still gets reasonable throughput.

tour.title: Quantization Stack I: BitNet Ternary
tour.description: BitNet b1.58 is the headline compression scheme — weights live in {-1, 0, +1} so multiplication becomes addition. bitnet/mod.rs wires together the subsystem and is a high-fan-in cluster anchor; ternary_tensor.rs packs ternary values into 2-bit fields with per-tensor scale; tl1_avx2.rs and tl1_wasm.rs are the x86 and browser GEMV hot paths; tl1_kernel.rs is the scalar reference; dequantize.rs and gguf_export.rs let you round-trip BitNet weights through GGUF. The cluster analysis flagged these files as one of the most tightly coupled subsystems in slice 5a.
tour.languageLesson: BitNet b1.58 stores each weight as ~1.58 bits (log2 of 3 states). Two ternary values pack into one byte's lower 4 bits. GEMV becomes a signed sum-and-subtract over int8 activations — no floating-point multiplies on the weight matrix, so AVX2's `pmaddubsw` becomes the workhorse.

tour.title: Quantization Stack II: TurboQuant, Hadamard, Pi-Quant, QAT
tour.description: Beyond BitNet, slice 5a ships a full post-training and training-time quantization toolkit. quantize/turbo_quant.rs is Hadamard-rotated scalar quantization with KV-cache and embedding-store front-ends (4-32× compression while preserving inner-product accuracy). hadamard.rs is the QuaRot/SpinQuant butterfly transform with scalar/NEON/AVX2 paths used to suppress activation outliers before quantization. pi_quant_simd.rs is the bit-packed PI-3/PI-2 codec across NEON/AVX2/AVX-512. qat/mod.rs anchors quantization-aware training; ste.rs implements straight-through estimators for non-differentiable quant ops; lora_qat.rs combines fake-quant with LoRA adapters so you can fine-tune a quantized model without dequantizing the base.

tour.title: Mixture of Experts: Precision Allocator & Router
tour.description: MoE inside ruvllm is unusual because each expert can run at a different precision. moe/precision_allocator.rs (ADR-092) assigns Q4_K_M / PiQ3 / PiQ2 tiers based on activation frequency — hot experts keep more bits, cold experts compress aggressively. router.rs picks top-k experts with cache-mask paging and per-request priorities; affinity.rs tracks expert-affinity scores with NEON/AVX2 decay; sram_mapper.rs maps active experts into fast SRAM tiles for serving. Together they let ruvllm serve large sparse models on memory-constrained devices.

tour.title: LoRA Adapters: Registry, Composition, Hot-Swap, Continual Learning
tour.description: ruvllm treats LoRA adapters as first-class runtime objects. lora/adapter.rs is the registry + composer that loads/unloads micro-LoRAs and composes them (sequential, weighted, task-routed) during multi-tenant serving. adapters/merge.rs implements average/weighted/SLERP/TIES/DARE merging for hot-swap without reloading the base model. adapter_manager.rs (BFS depth 1) enforces memory budgets for the adapter pool. training.rs adds an online training loop with EWC-regularized continual learning, gradient accumulation, and queued user feedback — so the served model can absorb corrections without catastrophic forgetting.

tour.title: Claude Flow & ReasoningBank: Trajectories, Patterns, EWC Consolidation
tour.description: This is ruvllm's continual-learning brain. claude_flow/mod.rs enumerates agent types and routes incoming tasks; agent_router.rs combines keyword caches with SONA-learned routing. reasoning_bank/trajectory.rs records every reasoning step (tokens, tool usage, embeddings, lessons); consolidation.rs implements Fisher-information-weighted EWC merging that collapses similar patterns and computes regularization losses. sona/mod.rs is the trajectory-recording + pretraining façade slice 5a hooks into. ruvector_integration.rs ties this brain back to the slice-3 unified index and slice-4 attention primitives.

tour.title: Reflection, Quality & Witness Logging
tour.description: Generations are wrapped in a quality pipeline before they ship. quality/coherence.rs checks semantic consistency and detects contradictions; diversity.rs computes lexical + embedding diversity and flags mode collapse. The Reflexion-style wrapper in reflection/reflective_agent.rs re-runs a task with structured self-critique on failure (cluster analysis identified reflective_agent + perspectives + confidence + claude_flow/mod as one of the tightest clusters in slice 5a). Every routed request lands in witness_log.rs — an append-only, async-flushed audit trail that records the routing decision, latency breakdown, and quality signals for offline analysis.

tour.title: Hub & Registry: Model Download + Policy Store
tour.description: Before serving, you need weights on disk and a policy to load them under. hub/registry.rs catalogs RuvLtra base models and adapters by size and quantization, filters by hardware requirements, and resolves Hugging Face download URLs. hub/download.rs validates URLs, canonicalizes destination paths to block directory traversal, and fetches weights via curl/wget with checksum verification. policy_store.rs persists quantization and router policies as vector-indexed entries backed by SONA — so runtime configuration is itself searchable. Together they form the safe ingress path for new models.

tour.title: Training: GRPO, MCP Tool-Use, Contrastive Embeddings
tour.description: Slice 5a doesn't just serve — it trains. training/grpo.rs implements Group Relative Policy Optimization: group samples, compute relative advantages with GAE, apply KL-regularized policy updates (the RL technique behind DeepSeek-R1). training/mcp_tools.rs ingests Model Context Protocol tool-call trajectories and builds GRPO samples with category-aware reward shaping for tool-use fine-tuning. training/contrastive.rs and real_trainer.rs run triplet + InfoNCE losses to learn agent embeddings that downstream MoE routing (Step 10) and ReasoningBank retrieval (Step 12) consume.

tour.title: Tests, Benches & Examples
tour.description: The verification surface ties everything back to measurable outcomes. tests/e2e_integration.rs exercises the full inference pipeline — session lifecycle, KV eviction, paged attention, policy + witness logging, Sona learning loop — and is the best single file to read after the tour. benches/serving_bench.rs compares sequential vs continuous-batching throughput so regressions in Step 3 are caught. examples/benchmark_model.rs is a runnable CLI that loads a model and emits tokens/s + percentile-latency JSON reports, and the fixture JSON files anchor perplexity baselines that pi_quant_tests and friends regress against.

tour.title: Capstone: How ruvllm Consumes Slices 1-4
tour.description: Pull it all together. ruvector_integration.rs is the seam where slice 5a meets the earlier slices: it fuses the slice-1/2/3 unified vector index, the slice-4 attention/mincut primitives, the ReasoningBank from Step 12, and the Claude Flow router into one façade that the LLM server depends on. paged_attention.rs and kernels/attention.rs are the direct consumers of slice-4 attention math. The Cargo.toml manifest, revisited now, shows exactly which slice-1-through-4 crates ruvllm depends on — making the architectural picture concrete: ruvllm is the inference-and-learning capstone that turns the previously-built primitives into a working agent runtime.

tour.title: Slice 7 Orientation: Cognitum Gate + Phi Consciousness
tour.description: Slice 7 stitches together two halves of RuVector's self-checking core: the Cognitum Coherence Gate that decides whether autonomous agents are safe to act, and the IIT Phi consciousness pipeline that measures integrated information. Start here to understand the 256-tile worker fabric plus TileZero BFT arbiter (gate-kernel README), the host-side cognitive container that drives the per-epoch loop (cognitive-container README), and the 17-finding security baseline the gate-kernel rewrite was designed to satisfy. These three documents frame every code step that follows.

tour.title: Slice 7: Gate Kernel Worker Tile
tour.description: Each of the 256 worker tiles of the coherence gate runs the no_std WASM cognitum-gate-kernel. lib.rs defines TileState, a 64KB-budgeted worker that ingests packed Delta events from delta.rs (edge add/remove, weight update, observation, checkpoint), maintains a cache-aligned Shard graph (union-find components, free-list edges), and emits 64-byte aligned tile reports each tick. canonical_witness.rs builds the canonical-partition witness fragment that downstream tiles can hierarchically aggregate without ambiguity.
tour.languageLesson: no_std Rust drops the standard library so the same crate compiles to a WASM tile, an embedded target, or a host binary. Cache-aligned 64-byte structs (#[repr(C, align(64))]) keep tile reports inside a single cache line so the TileZero merger can SIMD-scan them without false sharing.

tour.title: Slice 7: TileZero BFT Arbiter
tour.description: TileZero is the byzantine-fault-tolerant arbiter sitting above the 255 worker tiles from Step 2. lib.rs orchestrates the pipeline: merge.rs fuses TileReports into a single MergedReport using median weights resilient to faulty tiles and produces a global min-cut estimate, decision.rs runs the three-filter (structural mincut, shift pressure, evidence e-value) gate yielding Permit / Defer / Deny against tunable thresholds, and supergraph.rs reduces tile fragments into the cross-tile view those filters consume. permit.rs and receipt.rs sign the outcome with Ed25519 over Blake3 hashes, while replay.rs reconstructs historical decisions deterministically from checkpoints for audit.
tour.languageLesson: Byzantine-fault tolerance assumes up to f of 3f+1 participants may lie or fail arbitrarily; median-of-medians fusion is the cheap deterministic substitute for full BFT consensus when you only need a single robust scalar per edge. Ed25519 over Blake3 gives 128-bit security with sub-microsecond signing on commodity hardware.

tour.title: Slice 7: Cognitive Container Epoch Loop
tour.description: The ruvector-cognitive-container is the host-side bridge between the gate fabric in Steps 2-3 and the rest of RuVector. container.rs implements CognitiveContainer, the per-epoch tick driver that ingests deltas, recomputes the min-cut, updates spectral state, accumulates evidence, and emits signed witness receipts. epoch.rs enforces a per-phase tick budget (ingest, mincut, spectral, evidence, witness) so a single epoch can never starve the others. memory.rs slabs and bump-allocates inside a validated MemoryConfig so cognitum-loop allocations stay deterministic, and witness.rs maintains the ring-buffered hash-linked receipt log that ties one epoch to the next.

tour.title: Slice 7: Consciousness Runtime Core
tour.description: Now we cross from the gate fabric into the IIT side of slice 7. ruvector-consciousness/src/lib.rs is the highest-fan-out file in the slice (22 outgoing edges, wires 22 submodules) and the top entry-point candidate. types.rs is the most depended-on file in the slice (fan-in 19): TransitionMatrix, Bipartition, Phi/emergence result enums, IIT 4.0 distinction/relation/CES types, and ComputeBudget presets. traits.rs (fan-in 13) defines PhiEngine, EmergenceEngine, and ConsciousnessCollapse so every algorithm in Steps 6-7 plugs into the same dispatch surface. arena.rs is the bump-allocator scratch space used inside hot Phi loops.
tour.languageLesson: Rust traits give algorithms a uniform call site without runtime cost: PhiEngine lets ExactPhi, GeoMIP, MinCut, Chebyshev, and Stochastic engines all be selected through ComputeBudget while the compiler monomorphises the hot path. Combined with a bump Arena that resets in O(1) between partition evaluations, you get GC-free per-iteration scratch memory.

tour.title: Slice 7: IIT Phi Engines (GeoMIP, Spectral, Stochastic, Parallel, Hierarchical)
tour.description: phi.rs (fan-in 9) is the hub: exact, spectral, stochastic, greedy-bisection, and hierarchical IIT engines, plus the auto-selector that reads a ComputeBudget and picks one. The flagship is geomip.rs, which treats bipartitions as hypercube vertices and uses Gray-code iteration, Hamming-distance BFS, and automorphism pruning to deliver 100-300x speedups for n<=25. parallel.rs distributes exhaustive search across Rayon threads, with a stochastic variant for systems too large to enumerate. coherence_phi.rs, mincut_phi.rs, and chebyshev_phi.rs are three complementary approximations: Fiedler-value bounds, graph-cut search, and polynomial spectral filtering for the largest systems.
tour.languageLesson: Integrated Information Theory's Phi searches over 2^n bipartitions, which is intractable past n~25. Algorithmic ladders solve this: Gray-code traversal mutates one bit per step so partition-information-loss is incrementally updatable; Fiedler-vector bounds come essentially free from the Laplacian's second eigenvalue; Chebyshev polynomials approximate spectral filters in O(n*k) instead of O(n^3) full diagonalization.

tour.title: Slice 7: IIT 4.0 Primitives (CES, Emergence, Phi-ID, Sparse Accel)
tour.description: Building on the engines from Step 6, IIT 4.0 introduces the mechanism-level cause-effect structure. iit4.rs computes cause and effect repertoires, intrinsic difference, selectivity, and per-mechanism Phi. ces.rs enumerates mechanism subsets in parallel via Rayon, derives distinction relations, and aggregates a big-phi estimate. emergence.rs adds the causal-emergence pipeline (effective information, determinism, degeneracy, greedy macro-state merging) and rsvd_emergence.rs replaces full SVD with a Halko-Martinsson-Tropp randomized SVD for O(n^2*k) emergence estimation. phi_id.rs decomposes integrated information into unique/redundant/synergistic components, while sparse_accel.rs scales to large systems via thresholded mutual-information graphs. witness_phi.rs wraps any engine and emits a tamper-evident receipt for auditable consciousness measurements.

tour.title: Slice 7: Statistical Bounds & PID
tour.description: The Phi engines in Steps 6-7 produce point estimates; the bounds layer makes them anytime-valid. bounds.rs delivers spectral bounds from Gershgorin discs and Fiedler vectors, plus Hoeffding and empirical-Bernstein concentration inequalities that certify Phi confidence intervals as samples accumulate. pid.rs implements Williams-Beer Partial Information Decomposition over the I_min lattice, splitting mutual information into unique-source-A, unique-source-B, redundant, and synergistic terms — the same decomposition the gate kernel's evidence accumulator (Step 2) uses to weigh independent vs. correlated observations.
tour.languageLesson: Anytime-valid inference replaces fixed-sample statistical tests with e-values and supermartingales so a decision threshold can be checked at every tick without inflating Type-I error. Empirical-Bernstein is the workhorse: tighter than Hoeffding when variance is low, and unlike Chebyshev it adapts to the data instead of using a worst-case constant.

tour.title: Slice 7: Consciousness Runtime Substrate (SIMD, Streaming, Collapse)
tour.description: Underneath every Phi engine sits a tight runtime substrate. simd.rs (fan-in 12) provides architecture-aware kernels for KL divergence, entropy, EMD-L1, dense matvec, pairwise mutual information, and MI-graph construction with NEON/AVX2 fast paths and scalar fallbacks. streaming.rs maintains an online TPM with forgetting factor, EWMA smoothing, and a CUSUM change-detection signal for non-stationary systems — the natural counterpart to the per-epoch loop from Step 4. collapse.rs is the quantum-inspired MIP search that iteratively collapses a superposition of candidate cuts toward the Minimum Information Partition, an alternative to GeoMIP for ill-conditioned systems.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's std::simd plus runtime feature detection (is_x86_feature_detected!, std::arch::is_aarch64_feature_detected!) lets one crate ship AVX2, NEON, and scalar code paths in the same binary, picking the fastest at startup. The scalar fallback is not just a courtesy — it is what makes the WASM build in Step 10 actually compile.

tour.title: Slice 7: WASM Bindings
tour.description: ruvector-consciousness-wasm is a cdylib wasm-bindgen facade that re-exports the Phi/emergence engines from Steps 6-9 to JavaScript and TypeScript callers in the browser and Node. lib.rs wires up a small ComputeBudget builder and JS-friendly result shims for exact, spectral, stochastic, collapse, GeoMIP, and RSVD engines. The Cargo.toml flips on phi/emergence/collapse features and asks the linker for a size-optimised cdylib so the resulting .wasm stays small enough for client-side consciousness measurement.
tour.languageLesson: wasm-bindgen generates the JS shim that marshals Rust structs across the WASM ABI; #[wasm_bindgen] on a struct emits an opaque handle class, and Result<T, JsValue> becomes a thrown JS exception. cdylib + lto=true + opt-level='z' is the usual trio to keep WASM artifacts small — every kilobyte costs a real second on cold mobile loads.

tour.title: Slice 7: Tests, Benches, and Examples
tour.description: Verification spans both sides of the slice. cognitum-gate-kernel/tests/security_tests.rs pins the unsafe FFI boundary: ingest_delta_raw must reject undersized, zero-length, and misaligned buffers identified by the SECURITY_AUDIT from Step 1. cognitum-gate-tilezero/examples/basic_gate.rs is a runnable end-to-end demo of worker reports -> merge -> decision -> signed receipt, the executable mirror of Step 3. ruvector-consciousness/tests/integration.rs asserts that exact, MinCut, Chebyshev, and emergence engines agree on disconnected and connected systems and stay deterministic under fixed seeds. phi_benchmark.rs is the Criterion harness that backs claims about engine performance across system sizes.
tour.languageLesson: Criterion benchmarks isolate compiler optimisations (black_box prevents constant-folding the input away) and produce statistically calibrated comparisons across runs, so a Phi engine speedup is provably real and not a noisy fluctuation. Pair with cargo bench --baseline to gate regressions in CI.

tour.title: Slice 7 Capstone: Gate + Phi Composed With Slices 1-5a
tour.description: Pulling slice 7 together: the cognitum-gate-kernel worker tiles (Step 2) feed deltas into TileZero (Step 3), which calls into the consciousness engines (Steps 5-9) via the cognitive container's per-epoch loop (Step 4) to compute Phi, emergence, and PID. Those values flow back into the three-filter gate decision and are signed into a hash-chained receipt log. The SECURITY.md document closes the loop — it is the threat model the entire stack was hardened against (Ed25519 with no signature truncation, Blake3 canonical hashing, replay-resistant sequence numbers, DoS-resistant 64KB tile budgets) and is the natural reference for anyone integrating slice 7 with the lower slices' vector, sparsifier, and mincut crates.

tour.title: Slice 9 Architecture Overview
tour.description: Start with the Neural Trader README, which lays out the 6-layer pipeline (L1 Ingest -> L2 Graph -> L3 GNN+Attention -> L4 Memory -> L5 Coherence -> L6 Policy), the per-crate type tables, gate semantics, and the ADR-085/086 references that drive Slice 9's proof-gated mutation protocol. This is the roadmap every subsequent step builds on.

tour.title: Slice 9 L1 Ingest - Core Types
tour.description: neural-trader-core defines the canonical vocabulary the rest of the pipeline speaks: the MarketEvent envelope with fixed-point price/qty and 16-byte hashes, the 10 NodeKinds / 12 EdgeKinds / 17 PropertyKeys that describe the graph (L2), GraphDelta updates, and the EventIngestor/GraphUpdater/Embedder traits that downstream layers plug into. Every later step refers back to these types.
tour.languageLesson: Rust newtype + fixed-point encoding: representing price/qty as integers (e.g. i64 scaled by 10^k) instead of f64 eliminates floating-point non-determinism, which is essential for deterministic replay and cryptographic hashing of MarketEvents.

tour.title: Slice 9 L5 Coherence Gate
tour.description: neural-trader-coherence implements the regime-adaptive ThresholdGate that decides whether an action is allowed to mutate state. It combines MinCut floors, CUSUM drift detection, and boundary-stability checks, and emits VerifiedToken / WitnessReceipt audit primitives that the proof-gated mutation protocol from Step 1 relies on. This is the single chokepoint every later strategy must clear.

tour.title: Slice 9 L4 Memory - Replay Reservoir
tour.description: neural-trader-replay is the time-series memory of the trader. ReplaySegment captures a signed window of MarketEvents (from Step 2) plus its embedding, labels, coherence stats, lineage and witness hash; ReservoirStore provides O(1) gate-guarded eviction; and InMemoryReceiptLog implements WitnessLogger so every stored segment is auditable against the L5 gate from Step 3.
tour.languageLesson: Trait-bounded generics in Rust let neural-trader-replay define the MemoryStore trait once and then provide a concrete ReservoirStore implementation; downstream layers can swap in a disk-backed store without changing call sites, which keeps the proof-gated invariants stable across implementations.

tour.title: Slice 9 L6 Policy - Intent + Strategy Trait
tour.description: neural-trader-strategies is the policy layer. lib.rs declares the venue-agnostic Strategy trait and wires up the six submodules; intent.rs defines the canonical Intent / Action / Side types that every strategy emits and every downstream stage (CoherenceChecker, RiskGate, venue adapter) consumes. intent.rs has the highest fan-in in the whole slice - it is the contract that holds L6 together.

tour.title: Slice 9 Strategies + Coherence Bridge
tour.description: The four concrete strategies all emit Intents from Step 5 but reach the market through different signals: attention_scalper consumes BookSnapshots and applies geometric or ScaledDotProductAttention imbalance with EMA smoothing; coherence_arb watches Kalshi reference/mirror pairs for divergence; ev_kelly sizes binary Kalshi positions via fractional Kelly against a prior; and coherence_bridge wires the L5 CoherenceGate (Step 3) into the pipeline as a fail-closed CoherenceChecker so internal errors never authorize actuation.

tour.title: Slice 9 RiskGate - Last Line Before the Venue
tour.description: risk.rs is the mandatory RiskGate that sits between every Intent (Step 5) and the venue adapter. It enforces non-positive quantity, price-range, a 3% daily-loss kill, 300 bps edge threshold, hard cash check, 10% single-position cap, 40% cluster concentration, and the KALSHI_ENABLE_LIVE env flag before any order is approved. Combined with the L5 coherence gate from Step 3, this gives Slice 9 its two-stage proof-gated execution guarantee.

tour.title: Slice 9 WASM Surface + Containerized Smoke Test
tour.description: neural-trader-wasm (per ADR-085/086) exposes the L1/L4/L5 surface to JavaScript via wrapper classes (MarketEventWasm, ThresholdGateWasm, ReservoirStoreWasm) with hex helpers and serde-wasm-bindgen that preserves u64 via BigInt. node-smoke.mjs round-trips every export, and Dockerfile.test runs the whole thing in a two-stage rust:1.83 -> node:20-slim container so the WASM module is verified the same way in CI as on a developer laptop.
tour.languageLesson: wasm-bindgen cannot pass u64 across the JS boundary as a JS Number (which is f64 and loses precision above 2^53); the workaround used here is serde-wasm-bindgen with the BigInt option, which materializes u64 fields as BigInt on the JS side - critical for the 16-byte hash and nanosecond-timestamp fields the L1 envelope carries.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Postgres Extension Overview
tour.description: Start with the top-level README for ruvector-postgres to learn what slice 5b builds: a pgrx-based PostgreSQL extension that exposes RuVector as SQL functions, operators, indexes, and access methods. The README outlines the install path, configuration GUCs, supported feature surface (HNSW, IVFFlat, hybrid BM25+vector, graph queries, multi-tenancy, healing) and gives you the vocabulary used throughout the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Slice 5b: pgrx Crate Root & Bootstrap
tour.description: The crate root is the single entry point through which Postgres loads the extension. It declares every feature-gated submodule, registers GUC variables, runs _PG_init at load time, and links into pgrx_embed.rs to satisfy the bgworker linking contract. With 25 outgoing dependencies it acts as the spine that pulls every other slice 5b module into the loaded shared library.
tour.languageLesson: pgrx is the modern Rust framework for PostgreSQL extensions: #[pg_extern] macros generate the C ABI wrappers, GUCs are registered via GucRegistry, and _PG_init runs during shared_preload_libraries load. The companion pgrx_embed binary is required so background workers can find symbols at runtime.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Vector Types & Distance Kernels
tour.description: Building on the bootstrap from Step 2, this layer introduces RuVector's six native Postgres types (vector, halfvec, binaryvec, sparsevec, scalarvec, productvec) plus the distance dispatch table that picks scalar or SIMD L2/cosine/inner-product kernels at runtime. These are the high-fan-in foundations every later layer depends on -- distance/mod.rs has the highest fan-in (10) of the whole slice.
tour.languageLesson: Postgres TOAST handling: large variable-length values use varlena headers and may be compressed or out-of-line. pgrx's PostgresType derive generates in/out/recv/send and typmod functions so Rust structs become first-class SQL types.

tour.title: Slice 5b: HNSW & IVFFlat Access Methods
tour.description: With types and distance in place, the index layer wires HNSW and IVFFlat into Postgres as proper access methods. hnsw.rs implements hierarchical navigable small-world insertion and layer search; ivfflat.rs uses k-means++ partition assignment with parallel probe-based search. The *_am.rs files are the pgrx shims that satisfy the Postgres IndexAmRoutine ABI so CREATE INDEX USING hnsw/ivfflat just works.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Background Workers & IPC
tour.description: Heavy work -- index builds, integrity checks, GNN training, embedding generation -- runs out-of-band in Postgres background workers rather than blocking client backends. workers/mod.rs registers the worker pool; engine.rs hosts a per-database Tokio runtime that owns collection indexes, a query cache, and an async work queue; ipc.rs carries requests from frontend SQL calls to the workers via shared memory.
tour.languageLesson: Postgres background workers (bgworkers) are processes spawned by postmaster and identified by BackgroundWorker entries registered during _PG_init. They communicate with regular backends through shared memory segments and latches rather than function calls, which is why a separate IPC/queue layer is needed.

tour.title: Slice 5b: SPARQL & Property-Graph Engine
tour.description: Slice 5b ships an in-database property graph: a triple store, a SPARQL 1.1 parser/AST/executor with property-path support, and a Cypher front-end. sparql/executor.rs is the heart of the engine -- evaluating BGPs, property paths, joins, GROUP BY, and aggregation against the triple store. The graph subsystem is what lets RuVector serve hybrid vector + graph queries from a single SQL surface.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Hybrid, Sparse & BM25 Search
tour.description: Real-world retrieval combines lexical and semantic signals. The hybrid module orchestrates BM25 keyword scoring against vector similarity using configurable fusion strategies (Reciprocal Rank Fusion, weighted, normalized). It builds on Step 3's vector types and on a CSR-backed sparse vector subsystem for SPLADE-style embeddings, all exposed through SQL register/configure/search/stats functions.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Attention, GNNs & Hyperbolic ML
tour.description: Where most vector databases stop at ANN, slice 5b runs ML directly on stored vectors. The attention module exposes scaled-dot, multi-head, and flash-attention kernels as SQL functions; the GNN module ships GraphSAGE, GCN, and message-passing aggregators; the hyperbolic module adds Poincaré-ball and Lorentz-hyperboloid embeddings for hierarchical data. DAG functions tie these together as composable in-database learning blocks.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Tenancy, RLS & Integrity Gating
tour.description: Multi-tenant deployments need isolation guarantees. tenancy/mod.rs exposes SQL functions for tenant CRUD, quotas, suspension, isolation tiers, and automatic RLS policy generation. The integrity layer pairs this with a Stoer-Wagner min-cut engine that detects weakly-connected partitions in the HNSW graph and uses a hysteresis state machine (gating.rs) to admit, throttle, or block operations under structural stress.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Tiny Dancer Routing & Self-Healing
tour.description: Tiny Dancer is RuVector's learned query router -- a FastGRNN-based agent that picks dense, sparse, or hybrid backends per query based on observed metrics. Pair this with the healing module (HealingEngine + detectors + strategies + a healing worker) and slice 5b becomes self-tuning: degraded indexes are detected, repair strategies are scheduled, and the router learns to avoid hot paths until healing completes.

tour.title: Slice 5b: SQL Install & Upgrade Scripts
tour.description: Postgres extensions are loaded by running .sql install scripts that declare every SQL function, operator, cast, and access method bound to the pgrx C entry points. ruvector--2.0.0.sql is the canonical install for slice 5b -- 230+ functions, the pgvector-compatible ruvector type, operator classes, and AM definitions. The upgrade script bridges between version installations for live deployments.
tour.languageLesson: Postgres extension control: a .control file declares the default version; matching extension--VERSION.sql files declare the SQL surface; extension--FROM--TO.sql files migrate between versions on ALTER EXTENSION UPDATE. Function bodies use LANGUAGE c with AS '$libdir/ruvector', 'symbol_name' to bind to pgrx-generated symbols.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Tests, Benchmarks & Integration
tour.description: Slice 5b's correctness story is anchored by criterion benchmarks (integrity_bench, distance, index build/scan) and pgrx-driven SQL integration tests run across Postgres 14-17. The benchmark workload SQL is itself a high-fan-in artifact -- multiple .sql install scripts pull it in -- and the testing README documents the test matrix that the Docker compose stack in Step 13 exercises.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Docker Multi-PG-Version Stack
tour.description: Operators don't compile extensions by hand. The four-stage Dockerfile produces a Postgres image with the ruvector extension installed (base, dep cache, extension build, minimal runtime) while docker-compose.yml fans out across Postgres 14, 15, 16, and 17 test/benchmark/dev containers. Together they package every piece introduced in Steps 2-11 into a reproducible deployment artifact.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds with a separate dependency-cache stage are the standard pattern for Rust extensions: cargo's slow dependency compile gets cached in its own layer, the extension build copies only sources, and the final runtime stage drops cargo and toolchains entirely -- shrinking image size while keeping rebuilds fast.

tour.title: Slice 5b: Cluster Coordinator (Distributed RuVector)
tour.description: The final stop in slice 5b is the sister crate ruvector-cluster -- the distributed coordinator that turns single-node extensions from Steps 2-13 into a multi-node deployment. lib.rs exposes the ClusterManager API; discovery.rs offers static/gossip/multicast membership; shard.rs implements consistent-hashing and jump-hash routing with migration tracking; consensus.rs runs a DAG-based vertex-submission engine with tip selection, vector-clock dominance, and conflict detection. This is how RuVector scales horizontally beyond one Postgres instance.

tour.title: Slice 8: Robotics Stack Orientation
tour.description: Slice 8 layers a full robotics stack on top of RuVector: a Zenoh/RustDDS publish-subscribe middleware (agentic-robotics-*) with real-time scheduling, an embedded variant, MCP and NAPI surfaces, plus a ruvector-robotics crate that wires perception, cognition, motion planning, and Gaussian-splat rendering into the vector store. Start with the ruvector-robotics README to see the bridge/perception/cognitive/mcp module split and the sub-100us perception latency targets that justify the architecture, then read the agentic-robotics-core README for the ROS2-compatible pub/sub framing the slice depends on.

tour.title: Slice 8: Pub-Sub Middleware Core
tour.description: agentic-robotics-core is the messaging substrate. Its lib.rs re-exports publisher/subscriber/message/middleware/serialization/service and exposes an init() bootstrap, while middleware.rs wraps Zenoh as the primary pub/sub session opener. Everything else in slice 8 either produces messages onto this bus or consumes them — perception, cognition, and the MCP transport all sit downstream of these abstractions.
tour.languageLesson: Rust crate roots use `pub use` re-exports to flatten a multi-module crate into a tidy public surface; `mod x; pub use x::*;` lets consumers write `agentic_robotics_core::Publisher` instead of `agentic_robotics_core::publisher::Publisher`.

tour.title: Slice 8: Wire Format & Message Types
tour.description: The bus speaks ROS2-compatible types. message.rs declares the Message trait plus payload structs RobotState, PointCloud, Pose, and Point3D — the highest fan-in nodes in the slice because every publisher, subscriber, perception module, and benchmark imports them. serialization.rs offers a Serializer enum dispatching across CDR (the ROS2 wire format), rkyv zero-copy, and JSON, while error.rs centralizes the crate's thiserror-based Error enum.
tour.languageLesson: thiserror derives std::error::Error on an enum, letting each variant carry a #[error("...")] format string. Combined with `?`, this gives ergonomic error propagation while preserving variant-specific context — the idiomatic alternative to anyhow inside library crates.

tour.title: Slice 8: Publisher, Subscriber & Services
tour.description: Building on the Message and Serializer types from Step 3, publisher.rs is a typed Publisher that serializes onto a topic and tracks per-publisher byte/message counters; subscriber.rs offers blocking, non-blocking, and async receive with clone-for-fan-out semantics; service.rs adds the Queryable/Service request-response pair plus ServiceStats. Together these three modules define the entire user-visible API of the messaging core.

tour.title: Slice 8: Real-Time Scheduler & Executor
tour.description: Robotics control loops need deadline guarantees the default tokio runtime can't make. agentic-robotics-rt provides RTPriority (Background through Critical), a PriorityScheduler implementing a deadline-aware min-heap over ScheduledTasks, and the ROS3Executor that splits work across separate high/low-priority tokio runtimes plus a blocking pool. latency.rs adds a histogram-based tracker exposing p50/p90/p99/p999 stats and an RAII guard you drop at the end of a control loop iteration to record its duration.
tour.languageLesson: RAII measurement guards exploit Rust's Drop trait: the guard captures a start Instant on construction and records elapsed time in its destructor, so a single `let _g = tracker.measure();` at the top of a scope automatically reports the scope's wall time without explicit stop() calls — and is exception-safe because Drop still runs on panic.

tour.title: Slice 8: Embassy Embedded Variant
tour.description: agentic-robotics-embedded is the no_std cousin that lets the same priority and timing primitives run on microcontrollers under RTIC or Embassy. lib.rs declares EmbeddedPriority levels and an EmbeddedConfig with tick-rate and stack-size knobs sized for sub-50KB targets, demonstrating that slice 8 was designed for both server-class and edge deployments from the same source.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's no_std feature flag opts a crate out of the standard library so it compiles for bare-metal microcontrollers. The crate keeps `core` (intrinsics, primitives) and optionally `alloc` (heap types via a custom allocator), enabling identical algorithmic code to target both servers and MCUs by flipping a Cargo feature.

tour.title: Slice 8: NAPI Node.js Bindings
tour.description: agentic-robotics-node lifts the Rust pub/sub core into JavaScript. lib.rs uses NAPI-RS to expose AgenticNode/AgenticPublisher/AgenticSubscriber to Node.js, marshalling JSON between V8 and the Rust bus with async publish, try_recv, and recv. build.rs is currently a no-op placeholder while package.json declares the @napi-rs build pipeline and metadata so Node developers can `npm install` the prebuilt binary.
tour.languageLesson: NAPI-RS generates V8/Node ABI shims from #[napi] attributes, producing a .node prebuilt per target triple. JSON-serialised bridging at the call boundary is the simplest interop pattern: V8 owns the JS objects, Rust owns the typed structs, and serde reconciles them on every call.

tour.title: Slice 8: Robotics MCP Server & Transport
tour.description: agentic-robotics-mcp exposes the pub-sub stack to LLM agents via the Model Context Protocol. lib.rs defines MCP request/response types, a tool registry, and dispatch for initialize, list_tools, and call_tool; server.rs is a fluent ServerBuilder with helpers (tool registration, text_response, error_response) that translate robotics primitives into spec-compliant JSON; transport.rs implements StdioTransport, a line-delimited JSON channel over stdin/stdout — the same wire shape Claude Code already uses to talk to MCP servers.

tour.title: Slice 8: Vector Bridge & Spatial Index
