tour.description: ruvector-robotics begins where agentic-robotics-core ends: the bridge folder is where sensor data crosses into the vector store. bridge/mod.rs declares the shared primitives (Point3D, Quaternion, Pose, PointCloud, RobotState, SensorFrame, OccupancyGrid, SceneGraph, Trajectory) — the highest fan-in node in the slice. converters.rs marshals those primitives into RuVector vectors, indexing.rs builds a SpatialIndex with KNN and radius search across Euclidean/Manhattan/cosine metrics, search.rs defines the Neighbor/SearchResult/ObstacleAlert result types, and gaussian.rs packs point clouds into compact Gaussian splats for 3D viewer rendering.

tour.title: Slice 8: Perception Pipeline
tour.description: Perception turns raw frames into structured scene understanding. perception/mod.rs declares PerceptionPipeline orchestrating obstacle detection, scene graph construction, trajectory prediction, attention focusing, and anomaly detection. scene_graph.rs computes proximity-based scene graphs with semantic near/far edges and timestamp-preserving cross-frame merges; clustering.rs uses spatial hashing plus union-find to label point clouds; obstacle_detector.rs fits bounding extents and classifies obstacles as Static/Dynamic/Unknown; sensor_fusion.rs voxel-downsamples multi-sensor clouds; config.rs is the serde-roundtripped configuration glue.

tour.title: Slice 8: Cognition (Perceive-Think-Act-Learn)
tour.description: Above perception sits cognition. cognitive_core.rs implements the perceive-think-act-learn loop with attention-thresholded percept admission, confidence-ranked decision selection, emergency-mode preemption, and reward-driven threshold adaptation. world_model.rs tracks objects with kinematic prediction over a 2D occupancy grid; decision_engine.rs is a utility-based scorer over ActionOption candidates; behavior_tree.rs ticks Action/Condition/Sequence/Selector/Decorator/Parallel nodes against a blackboard; memory_system.rs gives a tri-layer working/episodic/semantic memory with cosine retrieval; skill_learning.rs grows a SkillLibrary from demonstrations; swarm_intelligence.rs adds multi-robot task assignment, formation control, and consensus voting.

tour.title: Slice 8: Planning, RVF Packing & Domain Expansion
tour.description: Three connective modules sit at the crate's edge. planning.rs implements A* search over the OccupancyGrid produced by the world model in Step 11 plus a reactive potential-field velocity controller and waypoint utilities. rvf.rs is the RuVector File packing layer that adapts robotics primitives (point clouds, scene objects, trajectories, Gaussian splats, obstacles) into the vector store with strict dimension enforcement and kNN passthrough. domain_expansion.rs defines a RoboticsDomain task generator covering clustering, avoidance, scene graph, skill sequencing, and swarm formation — used by evaluation harnesses to score robotics behaviour.

tour.title: Slice 8: Robotics MCP Tools
tour.description: The robotics MCP module is the agent-facing capstone of ruvector-robotics. mcp/mod.rs declares tool parameters, schemas, the RoboticsToolRegistry, and register_defaults that populates ~30 robotics tools (perceive, plan, swarm, learn) for AI-assistant orchestration. mcp/executor.rs is the dispatcher: it routes LLM JSON requests to PerceptionPipeline methods like detect_obstacles, build_scene_graph, predict_trajectory, focus_attention, detect_anomalies, spatial_search, and insert_points, recording per-call latency for the same histograms introduced in Step 5.

tour.title: Slice 8: Examples, Benchmarks & Integration
tour.description: Close the tour with the runnable artefacts that exercise everything above end-to-end. examples/cognitive_loop.rs drives the full perceive-think-act-learn cycle on synthetic input; swarm_coordination.rs registers robots with a SwarmCoordinator, assigns tasks, and runs consensus; obstacle_detection.rs, behavior_tree.rs, and spatial_indexing.rs are minimal demos for the named subsystems. tests/robotics_integration.rs is a 20-test suite covering perception, memory, behaviour trees, swarm, MCP tool calls, Gaussian splatting, A* and potential-field planning, sensor fusion, and concurrent spatial search. agentic-robotics-benchmarks/benches/pubsub_latency.rs measures Zenoh/RustDDS publish latency, throughput, end-to-end latency, CDR-vs-JSON cost, and concurrent-publisher scaling on the messaging core from Steps 2-4.

tour.title: Slice 6c: rvm Microhypervisor Overview
tour.description: Start with the rvm crate-level README, the architecture roadmap doc, and the workspace Cargo.toml. rvm is a coherence-native, no_std AArch64 microhypervisor whose workspace stitches 13 internal crates (types, hal, cap, witness, proof, partition, sched, memory, coherence, boot, wasm, security, kernel) into a single hypervisor image. These three artifacts establish the partition-based architecture, the capability/witness/proof trust chain, and the crate map you will walk through over the next several steps.

tour.title: Slice 6c: Bare-Metal Boot & AArch64 HAL
tour.description: Bring-up begins with rvm-boot's measured boot tracker, the entry-point that hashes each phase into a boot digest chain, and the rvm-hal AArch64 barrel that exposes boot, MMU, timer, interrupts, and UART submodules. This is the only place in the hypervisor where unsafe is permitted — every architecture-specific MSR write, MMU table setup, and exception-vector install lives behind this HAL boundary. The Makefile and QEMU targets later in the tour run exactly this entry point on virt machines.
tour.languageLesson: no_std Rust crates omit the standard library and target bare-metal environments. Symbols normally provided by std (panic handler, allocator, eh_personality) must be supplied by the binary or a downstream crate, which is why rvm-boot, rvm-hal and friends compose into rvm-kernel rather than running standalone.

tour.title: Slice 6c: rvm-types Domain Vocabulary
tour.description: rvm-types is the shared type-system crate every other rvm crate imports from. Its lib.rs re-exports addr, capability, coherence, config, device, error, ids, memory, partition, proof, recovery, scheduler, and witness modules so that PartitionId, CapabilityId, MemoryRegion, and the various error enums are defined in exactly one place. Understanding this vocabulary up front makes every subsequent crate's API readable at a glance.

tour.title: Slice 6c: Capability System (ADR-135 P1)
tour.description: rvm-cap implements the first layer (P1) of the three-layer proof model from ADR-135. The capability table uses slot-based storage with generation counters to prevent use-after-free, and the derivation tree tracks parent/child relationships so revoking a parent atomically revokes every descendant. Every privileged operation in the hypervisor must present a valid capability before any policy or proof checking even runs.
tour.languageLesson: Generation counters are the no_std analogue of weak references: each slot pairs a payload with a monotonically-increasing counter, and capability handles store the generation they were minted at. Lookups that don't match the current generation return CapabilityRevoked instead of dereferencing a recycled slot, preventing use-after-free without needing an allocator-backed reference count.

tour.title: Slice 6c: Partition Object Model (ADR-133)
tour.description: rvm-partition defines the Partition aggregate per ADR-133 — lifecycle states, partition-type taxonomy, local cut pressure, and the IpcManager / CommEdge types that model inter-partition communication. The crate root re-exports the CapabilityTable from Step 4 alongside PartitionManager, making clear that partitions are the unit of isolation, capability scoping, and coherence-graph membership. Cut pressure recorded here feeds the coherence engine two steps later.

tour.title: Slice 6c: Four-Tier Memory & Reconstruction (ADR-136/137)
tour.description: rvm-memory layers a Hot/Warm/Dormant/Cold tier manager (ADR-136) on top of region allocation and permission tracking. Tiering decisions are driven by coherence cut-value plus recency, so memory follows the same signal that drives scheduling. The reconstruction module (ADR-137) checkpoints partition memory and replays witness-delta logs to rebuild state after a fault, tying memory directly into the witness logging subsystem two steps ahead.

tour.title: Slice 6c: Stoer-Wagner Coherence Engine (ADR-132)
tour.description: rvm-coherence is the conceptual heart of the slice. The coherence graph treats partitions as nodes and communication frequency as weighted edges; the Stoer-Wagner min-cut implementation finds the cheapest split each epoch, and the CoherenceEngine combines that with adaptive pressure analysis to recommend merge/split/migrate decisions to the scheduler. This is what makes rvm coherence-native rather than priority-native.
tour.languageLesson: Stoer-Wagner finds a global minimum cut of an undirected weighted graph in O(V*E + V^2 log V) without any explicit source/sink. Each phase performs a maximum-adjacency ordering, records the last-added vertex as one side of a candidate cut, and contracts it with the previous vertex; the cheapest candidate across all phases is the answer. For a hypervisor scheduler this means 'the natural fault line between hot communication clusters' falls out of the algorithm without operator hints.

tour.title: Slice 6c: Coherence-Gated Scheduler (ADR-132 DC-4)
tour.description: rvm-sched consumes the cut decisions from Step 7 and translates them into per-CPU scheduling under SMP. The crate root wires modes, priority, per-CPU state, epoch boundaries, context-switch primitives, and a degraded fallback path for when the coherence engine itself is unavailable. Together with rvm-coherence, this implements design choice DC-4 from ADR-132: the scheduler is downstream of coherence, not parallel to it.

tour.title: Slice 6c: Witness Log (ADR-134)
tour.description: rvm-witness is the append-only audit substrate the rest of the hypervisor writes through. ADR-134 fixes the 64-byte record format and FNV-1a hash chain so the log is tamper-evident even without external signing; the crate also exposes emitter, log, replay queries, and pluggable signer implementations. Every privileged decision the security gate makes in Step 11 leaves a witness record here.

tour.title: Slice 6c: TEE Proof Engine (ADR-142 P3)
tour.description: rvm-proof is the deferred (P3) verification layer of the ADR-135 proof model and the realisation of ADR-142 phase 2. The signer trait abstracts over HMAC-SHA256, Ed25519, dual-HMAC and Null implementations so witnesses can be authenticated by whichever crypto a board ships with, and the engine verifies plain, capability-bound, and signed proof witnesses, emitting structured proof-witness or proof-rejected events. This crate is where the TEE provider integration lives.

tour.title: Slice 6c: SecurityGate (P1+P2+P3 Funnel)
tour.description: rvm-security fuses the previous three steps into one thing — a SecurityGate that funnels every privileged hypercall through P1 capability check, P2 policy decision, and optional P3 chain verification, emitting a witness record on both allow and reject paths. This is the single chokepoint where capability, policy, and proof become indivisible: bypassing any one of them requires bypassing the gate, and the gate is the only API the kernel exposes to guests.

tour.title: Slice 6c: Per-Partition WASM Guests (ADR-140)
tour.description: rvm-wasm runs untrusted guest code as WebAssembly modules inside each partition. validate_module performs a header + LEB128 scan to reject malformed modules before load; the AgentManager implements the ADR-140 badge-derived AgentId and state machine (Initializing/Running/Suspended/Migrating/Hibernated/Reconstructing/Terminated) with every transition logged through the witness subsystem from Step 9. The quota module enforces per-epoch CPU, memory-page, and IPC budgets so a runaway agent can't starve its neighbours.
tour.languageLesson: LEB128 (Little-Endian Base 128) is the variable-length integer encoding used throughout the WebAssembly binary format: each byte contributes 7 bits of payload with the top bit acting as a continuation flag. A safe LEB128 decoder bounds the byte count (a u32 needs at most 5 bytes, a u64 at most 10) to defeat denial-of-service via runaway varints.

tour.title: Slice 6c: rvm-kernel Integration & QEMU Bring-Up
tour.description: rvm-kernel is the integration capstone — it wires HAL, capabilities, witness, proof, partitions, scheduler, memory, coherence, boot, WASM, and security into a single Kernel API consumed by the boot entry from Step 2. The Makefile drives the bare-metal build with the rvm.ld linker script and runs the image under QEMU virt for tests, objdump, and interactive bring-up, while the GitHub Actions workflow keeps cargo check / test green on every push.
tour.languageLesson: A linker script (rvm.ld) tells the linker exactly where each section (.text, .rodata, .data, .bss, stack, vector table) lives in physical memory. For bare-metal AArch64 you typically place the entry point at a fixed load address (often 0x40080000 for QEMU virt), align the exception vector table to 0x800, and reserve a BSS region the boot code can zero before Rust takes over.

tour.title: Slice 6c: rvlite — WASM-Shipped Lite Database
tour.description: Pivot now to the second half of the slice. rvlite is a standalone vector + triple store derived from RuVector but built cdylib+rlib so it compiles to WASM for browser, edge, and mobile targets without requiring Postgres. lib.rs is the public surface — it owns configuration, error types, and the dispatcher that routes SQL, Cypher, and SPARQL queries to the per-engine subsystems we explore next. The storage/epoch module reconciles RVF persistence epochs with metadata on open, picking rollback / replay / reconcile actions.

tour.title: Slice 6c: SQL / Cypher / SPARQL Tri-Engine
tour.description: rvlite ships three query engines side by side. The SQL parser is a hand-written tokenizer + recursive-descent parser handling SELECT/INSERT/CREATE/DROP plus vector literals. The Cypher subsystem exposes a wasm-bindgen CypherEngine wrapping lexer/parser/executor over an in-memory property graph and bridging to persisted state. The SPARQL executor evaluates SELECT/CONSTRUCT/ASK/DESCRIBE/UPDATE against a triple store with full BGP matching, joins, filters and aggregates — all dispatched from the lib.rs surface in Step 14.

tour.title: Slice 6c: rvlite Dashboard Demo (WASM in the Browser)
tour.description: The capstone is the dashboard example — a single-file React SPA (App.tsx, 4000+ lines) that loads the rvlite WASM build directly in the browser and orchestrates SQL/SPARQL/Cypher consoles, metrics panels, a filter builder, and a learning-engine integration. It is the user-facing proof that the same tri-engine from Step 15 runs unchanged outside any server. The Tailwind + Vite tooling shows the recommended packaging path for downstream rvlite consumers.
tour.languageLesson: wasm-bindgen + cdylib lets a Rust crate compile to a .wasm artifact paired with auto-generated JS glue that marshals strings, objects, and typed arrays across the JS/WASM boundary. Loading is usually async (init() returns a Promise) because browsers stream-compile the module; once initialised, exported Rust functions look like ordinary async JS functions, which is exactly how App.tsx talks to rvlite.

tour.title: What is rvf — workspace overview
tour.description: Start at the top: the rvf workspace Cargo manifest and README declare the ~26 sub-crates that make up the RuVector Format family. This step orients you to the federation of types, wire, manifest, index, runtime, server, CLI, adapters, and tooling crates the rest of the tour visits.

tour.title: Types & schemas — the shared vocabulary
tour.description: rvf-types is the foundation every other crate depends on: shared structs, schemas, quality metrics, and ADR-anchored primitives (ADR-031 reference counting, ADR-033 quality bands, ADR-036 AGI container). Read this before anything else — almost every later step refers back to these types.

tour.title: Wire protocol — segments, varints, hash dispatch
tour.description: rvf-wire defines how rvf-types are serialized on the wire: segment codecs, varint encoding, and hash-based dispatch. Both the runtime and the manifest layer speak this protocol, so understanding the segment layout here unlocks the storage and network surfaces.

tour.title: Storage format — Level-0 / Level-1 manifests
tour.description: rvf-manifest is the on-disk format: Level-0 readers/writers materialize raw segments while Level-1 layers structure and indexing on top. Combined with the wire codecs from Step 3, this is how rvf files persist and are re-opened by the runtime.

tour.title: Quantization — scalar, product, binary, sketches
tour.description: rvf-quant compresses high-dimensional vectors before they hit the index: scalar, product, and binary quantization plus probabilistic sketches. These primitives feed both the index and the runtime's memory budget, so they precede the index step.

tour.title: Index — progressive HNSW
tour.description: rvf-index is RuVector's progressive HNSW implementation: graph construction, traversal, and persistence. It consumes quantized vectors from Step 5 and is the engine that powers similarity search at the runtime layer.

tour.title: Cryptography — SHAKE-256, Ed25519, witness chains
tour.description: rvf-crypto provides the integrity and provenance layer: SHAKE-256 hashing, Ed25519 signatures, and the witness/lineage chains that bind manifests to their authors. The runtime weaves these primitives through every mutation to produce verifiable history.

tour.title: Runtime core — RvfStore, CoW, FFI, QR seeds
tour.description: rvf-runtime is the glue: RvfStore composes types, wire, manifest, quant, index, and crypto into a coherent store with copy-on-write semantics, a stable FFI surface, and QR-seeded sessions per ADR-033/036. Everything above this point is a transport for what this layer exposes.

tour.title: HTTP server — Axum surface
tour.description: rvf-server wraps the runtime in an Axum HTTP API. Routes mirror RvfStore operations so a remote caller can drive the same primitives the CLI uses locally — this is the first networked face of rvf.

tour.title: CLI — clap subcommands
tour.description: rvf-cli is the operator-facing entry point: clap subcommands map onto runtime calls for ingest, search, verify, and admin tasks. Reading the subcommand modules reveals the daily-driver shape of the system.

tour.title: Federation — ADR-057 aggregation & differential privacy
tour.description: rvf-federation implements ADR-057: federated aggregation across nodes with differential-privacy noise mechanisms and Byzantine tolerance. It builds on the runtime and crypto layers to combine partial results without leaking per-node data.

tour.title: WASM microkernel — cdylib exports
tour.description: rvf-wasm compiles a minimal runtime subset as a cdylib for browser and host embedding. The exported FFI surface lets external embedders drive rvf without linking the full Rust runtime — useful for sandboxed and edge deployments.

tour.title: eBPF + microkernel + launcher — the sandboxed pipeline
tour.description: Three cooperating layers sandbox rvf workloads: rvf-ebpf compiles eBPF programs, rvf-kernel packs them into a CPIO microkernel pipeline, and rvf-launch boots a QEMU microVM and drives it over QMP. Together they form rvf's hardened execution path.

tour.title: Adapters — agentdb, agentic-flow, claude-flow, ospipe, rvlite, sona
tour.description: The adapter crates bridge rvf to neighbouring systems: AgentDB persistence, agentic-flow / claude-flow agent runtimes, ospipe IPC, rvlite embedded variant, and sona. Each adapter is a thin translation layer — read them to see how rvf plugs into a larger toolchain.

tour.title: Integration tests — the capstone
tour.description: crates/rvf/tests exercises the whole stack end-to-end: ingest, manifest persistence, indexed search, signed witnesses, federation, and adapter round-trips. These tests are the executable specification — when you finish the tour, run them to see every prior step interacting in one process.

tour.title: What is rvAgent — workspace overview
tour.description: rvAgent is RuVector's production Rust agent runtime, a workspace of 10 sub-crates that compose into a full agent stack: core types, model backends, tools, MCP, middleware, A2A, ACP, sub-agent orchestration, a CLI, and a WASM runtime. Start at the top-level Cargo manifest and README to see how those pieces are declared and the persona specs (.ruv/agents) that ship with it.

tour.title: Agent core foundations — AgentState, Messages, ChatModel, RVF
tour.description: rvagent-core is the contract layer every other crate builds on: AgentState carries conversation history, RvAgentConfig binds defaults, Messages are the chat-model wire format, the ChatModel trait abstracts LLM providers, and the RVF bridge wires agent state into RuVector's verifiable format. Read this before anything else — Steps 3-11 all consume these primitives.

tour.title: Backends — Anthropic/Gemini clients and sandboxes
tour.description: rvagent-backends implements the ChatModel trait from Step 2 for live LLM providers (Anthropic, Gemini) and provides the filesystem + local-shell sandboxes that tools execute against. These are the I/O frontier: every model call and every side-effect leaves the agent through here.

tour.title: Tools — Tool trait, BuiltinTool dispatch, 9 implementors
tour.description: rvagent-tools defines the Tool trait and the BuiltinTool/AnyTool dispatch surface that the agent uses to call out to the world. Nine concrete tool implementors (read/write/edit files, shell, search, etc.) build on the backend sandboxes from Step 3 and produce structured results that flow back into AgentState.

tour.title: MCP — Model Context Protocol client and server
tour.description: rvagent-mcp is rvAgent's Model Context Protocol surface: an McpClient that talks to external MCP servers and a built-in axum-based MCP server with SSE and stdio transports, including middleware hooks. This is how rvAgent both consumes external tools and exposes its own tools to other agents.

tour.title: Middleware stack — 15 variants from HITL to witness chains
tour.description: rvagent-middleware wraps chat-model calls and tool invocations with 15 composable variants: human-in-the-loop approvals, retry/backoff, conversation summarization, witness-chain attestation, rate limits, logging, and more. Each middleware sees the AgentState from Step 2 and can short-circuit or transform requests before they reach a backend.

tour.title: A2A — Agent-to-Agent protocol (ADR-159)
tour.description: rvagent-a2a implements ADR-159 Agent2Agent: an A2aServer with task routing, push webhooks, SSE streams, and a budget ledger that bounds spend across collaborating agents. It transports the same AgentState/Message types from Step 2 between independent rvAgent instances.

tour.title: ACP — Agent Connect Protocol
tour.description: rvagent-acp wraps an rvAgent in the Agent Connect Protocol: AcpAgent presents the canonical agent interface and AcpServer hosts it. ACP is the cross-runtime contract — it lets non-rvAgent clients drive an agent without speaking A2A or MCP directly.

tour.title: Sub-agents and orchestration — builder, CRDT merge, orchestrator
tour.description: rvagent-subagents is where one agent spawns and coordinates many: a fluent builder constructs child agents, an orchestrator schedules them, and CRDT merge logic reconciles their AgentStates back into the parent. This is the hierarchical-mesh topology from CLAUDE.md, expressed in code.

tour.title: CLI — rvagent binary with TUI
tour.description: rvagent-cli is the operator-facing entry point: a clap-driven binary with a TUI for live interaction. The subcommands map onto the orchestrator, tools, and backends from prior steps, so reading the command modules is the fastest way to see how a real rvAgent session is wired end-to-end.

tour.title: WASM agent runtime — WasmAgent, WasmMcpServer, RVF builder
tour.description: rvagent-wasm compiles the agent runtime as a cdylib for sandboxed embedding: WasmAgent runs the core loop, WasmMcpServer exposes MCP from inside WASM, the gallery catalogs prebuilt agents, and the RVF builder serializes agent state into RuVector's verifiable format. This is the capstone — every prior layer reappears here, but constrained to a sandbox.

tour.title: What is ruvix? The Microhypervisor at a Glance
tour.description: Start with the top-level RuVix workspace: a no_std, capability-based Rust microhypervisor with 17 syscalls, six kernel primitives, three proof tiers, and 26 sub-crates. The README explains motivation versus Linux/seL4/Zephyr, and the workspace Cargo.toml enumerates every member crate you'll meet later in the tour.

tour.title: Typed Handles and Kernel ABI
tour.description: Before any subsystem can talk to another, every kernel object needs a stable identity. ruvix-types defines the 64-bit Handle (id+generation), the ObjectType discriminator, the KernelError ABI, and the Capability/Proof/Region/Task handles every other crate imports — making this the single most fan-in-heavy file in the slice.

tour.title: Hardware Abstraction Layer
tour.description: ruvix-hal defines the architecture-agnostic seams the kernel depends on: Console, InterruptController, Mmu, Timer, and PowerManagement traits. Concrete drivers in later steps implement these traits, so the kernel never names a CPU architecture directly.

tour.title: ARM64 Implementation & BCM2711 Drivers
tour.description: These two crates land the HAL traits on real silicon. ruvix-aarch64 installs the EL1 vector base, configures SCTLR/TCR/MAIR, and provides exception handlers; ruvix-bcm2711 supplies Raspberry Pi 4 peripherals — Mini UART console, mailbox, GPIO, and the BCM interrupt controller — built on volatile MMIO primitives.

tour.title: Pi Boot & Device Tree Discovery
tour.description: Before the kernel starts, rpi-boot drops EL2->EL1, configures the MMU/TLB, parks secondary CPUs in the spin table, and parses the kernel command line. The ruvix-dtb crate then walks the Flattened Device Tree (zero-allocation) to discover hardware topology that the boot pipeline turns into capabilities.

tour.title: The 5-Stage Boot Pipeline
tour.description: ruvix-boot orchestrates the canonical bring-up: Hardware probe -> Verify ML-DSA-65 signature -> Create tasks -> Mount RVF regions -> Attest. BootLoader drives the stages and emits a BootResult containing root capabilities, an attestation chain (rolling SHA-256), and an append-only witness log — establishing the trusted base every later step relies on.

tour.title: The Capability System
tour.description: ruvix-cap implements the security spine: a CapabilityManager grants/revokes Handle-tagged tokens, a derivation tree enables cascading revocation, and Grant validation enforces rights monotonicity and delegation depth. Boot.rs seeds the root task's initial capability set per ADR-087 §6.3; the audit module periodically scans for orphans and over-broad rights.

tour.title: Proof Engine & Tier Router
tour.description: ruvix-proof gates every mutation behind a tiered proof: Reflex (<10us), Standard (~100us), or Deep (~1ms). The ProofEngine generates tokens, the tier router selects a tier per mutation context, the ProofVerifier checks capabilities and caches results with TTL+nonce uniqueness, and witness.rs produces Merkle inclusion proofs that flow back into the boot witness log.

tour.title: Memory: Physmem, Regions, DMA
tour.description: Three crates compose the memory story. ruvix-physmem is a buddy allocator over physical frames; ruvix-region adds policy-gated virtual regions (Immutable / AppendOnly / Slab) on top of pluggable MemoryBacking implementations; ruvix-dma exposes a platform-agnostic DmaController trait with channels, descriptors, and cache-coherent buffers for high-throughput device transfers.

tour.title: Scheduler: EDF + Novelty + Risk
tour.description: ruvix-sched is the coherence-aware scheduler from ADR-087 §5. PartitionManager round-robins between partitions with time slices; within a partition the priority formula combines EDF deadline urgency, a centroid-based novelty boost (EMA-updated), and a structural-risk penalty. Task control blocks track Ready/Running/Blocked/Terminated lifecycle plus the coherence delta the proof engine consumes.

tour.title: Queues, FS, and Network — Kernel Services
tour.description: Three service crates sit above the memory and scheduler layers. ruvix-queue provides lock-free SPSC RingBuffers wrapped in KernelQueues for inter-task IPC; ruvix-fs exposes a VFS with FAT32 + RamFs over a BlockDevice trait; ruvix-net is a minimal Ethernet/ARP/IPv4/UDP/ICMP stack composed over a NetworkDevice trait.

tour.title: VecGraph: Kernel-Resident Cognition Store
tour.description: ruvix-vecgraph is what makes ruvix a *cognition* kernel: a vector store with SIMD distance kernels (NEON/AVX2/scalar) and an HNSW index, plus a graph store of nodes and edges. Both stores enforce proof_policy on every mutation, track per-vector coherence, and append signed attestations to a witness log that ties back to the proof engine from Step 8.

tour.title: SMP: Multi-Core Primitives
tour.description: ruvix-smp wires the kernel for up to 256 cores. CpuId/CpuState track per-CPU lifecycle on an atomic state machine; PerCpu<T> with CacheAligned wrappers avoid false sharing; ticket-based fair spinlocks provide FIFO mutual exclusion; and the IPI layer dispatches IpiMessages across GICv3 with stats. Barriers wrap DMB/DSB/ISB/SEV for portable ordering.

tour.title: Nucleus: The 17-Syscall Surface
tour.description: ruvix-nucleus is the integration crate: the Kernel object aggregates capabilities, regions, scheduler, vector/graph stores, witness log, and proof engine into one place. syscall.rs defines the ADR-087 17-syscall set (spawn / cap_grant / region_map / queue / timer / vector / graph / sensor / checkpoint / witness / ...), and Checkpoint+ReplayEngine give deterministic snapshot/replay.

tour.title: Operating ruvix: Shell, Host CLI, and the Cognitive Demo
tour.description: The capstone closes the loop. ruvix-shell exposes a 13-command in-kernel debug shell via the ShellBackend trait (the most fan-in-heavy trait in the slice). The host ruvix-cli drives the device — build / flash / monitor / dtb / keys / security. The cognitive_demo example wires SensorAdapter -> FeatureExtractor -> ReasoningEngine -> Attestor -> Coordinator over queues, exercising proof-gated VecGraph mutations end-to-end, and the integration-tests crate validates ADR-087 §17 acceptance.

tour.title: Cognition cluster: workspace overview
tour.description: Slice 10b spans four cooperating crates that together form RuVector's cognition stack: Prime Radiant (sheaf-Laplacian coherence engine), the Nervous System primitives, its WASM bindings, and Sona (continual-learning trainer). Start at the per-crate READMEs to anchor the vocabulary used throughout the rest of the tour.

tour.title: Prime Radiant: sheaf Laplacian engine
tour.description: The cohomology module is the mathematical heart of Prime Radiant — it builds sheaves over the substrate graph, computes restriction maps, and drives the Laplacian/diffusion solver that measures attentional coherence. The neural.rs adapter and SheafCoherenceValidator wire that math into runtime attention.

tour.title: Prime Radiant: distributed Raft replication
tour.description: To keep coherence state consistent across a cluster, Prime Radiant wraps its CoherenceStateMachine in a Raft replication layer. The adapter translates CoherenceCommand log entries into deterministic state transitions, while distributed/state.rs holds the replicated graph.

tour.title: Prime Radiant: GPU kernels and dispatch
tour.description: When the sheaf graph gets large, coherence is offloaded to the GPU through a wgpu pipeline. device.rs picks an adapter, buffer.rs/engine.rs manage VRAM, dispatch.rs schedules workgroups, and kernels.rs holds the compute shaders that implement the Laplacian on-device.

tour.title: Prime Radiant: governance, witnesses, and lineage
tour.description: Every coherence decision is auditable. The governance module defines PolicyBundles that gate execution, while WitnessRecord and LineageRecord (plus the ruvllm_integration witness log) provide cryptographic provenance for each generation step, persisted through a repository abstraction.

tour.title: Nervous System: neural primitives
tour.description: The Nervous System crate provides biologically-inspired building blocks that downstream crates compose. Winner-take-all competition, dendritic compartments with coincidence/plateau detection, a sharded eventbus, hyperdimensional computing (HDC) vectors, and Hopfield attractor memory together form the substrate for cognition.

tour.title: Nervous System: integration & collection versioning
tour.description: These primitives are stitched into RuVector's vector store through integration tests that exercise collection versioning, throughput, and end-to-end retrieval. The integration test files are the load-bearing examples of how NervousVectorIndex-style code composes WTA, HDC, and Hopfield against a real collection.

tour.title: Nervous System: plasticity (BTSP, EWC, replay)
tour.description: Plasticity rules let the system learn without catastrophic forgetting. BTSP supplies one-shot behavioral-time-scale potentiation, EWC adds Fisher-weighted consolidation, and a replay buffer interleaves rehearsals. The ewc_tests file is the canonical reference for how Fisher information, replay, and reward-modulated consolidation interact.

tour.title: Nervous System: routing & global workspace
tour.description: Cognitive routing decides which content reaches conscious processing. A Miller's-Law-bounded GlobalWorkspace arbitrates salience-based competition, an oscillatory router gates information by phase, and workspace_integration ties these into the registry that holds active cognitive content.

tour.title: Sona: continual learning core (EWC + LoRA + reasoning bank)
tour.description: Sona is the trainer that adapts language-model weights on the fly. lora.rs supplies low-rank micro-adapters for fast per-task updates, ewc.rs protects prior knowledge with Fisher penalties, and reasoning_bank.rs stores reusable reasoning trajectories that the engine pulls from during fine-tuning.

tour.title: Sona: training pipelines (instant, background, federated)
tour.description: Two learning loops run side-by-side: an instant loop applies micro-LoRAs within a single turn, while a background loop consolidates knowledge into the base adapter. A coordinator schedules between them, the training pipeline + factory build trainers, and federated.rs aggregates updates across peers.

tour.title: Nervous System WASM bindings
tour.description: The WASM crate exposes the cognition primitives to JavaScript so the browser can drive BTSP plasticity, HDC encoding, WTA competition, and the GlobalWorkspace directly. lib.rs is the wasm-bindgen surface; the per-module files are thin idiomatic wrappers over the Rust core covered earlier.

tour.title: Satellite Cluster Overview
tour.description: Slice 10f groups RuVector's 46 satellite crates — small, focused packages that wrap the core engine for specific deployment targets (browser WASM, Node.js, FFI, CLI) and specialized domains (attention, mincut, RaBitQ, thermal). Start here with the headline READMEs of the WASM core and routing crates to see how a satellite is structured: a thin Cargo.toml, a lib.rs surface, and a published pkg/README documenting the JS/host-side API.

tour.title: WASM Cores — Primitive Bindings
tour.description: The WASM cores expose RuVector's foundational primitives to browser hosts: micro-hnsw-wasm packages the standalone HNSW index, ruvector-cnn-wasm exports a contrastive embedder with InfoNCE/Triplet losses and SIMD ops, and ruvector-dag-wasm surfaces the DAG engine. Each crate uses wasm-bindgen to project Rust structs (MicroHnsw, WasmCnnEmbedder) into JavaScript classes with explicit init() and per-op methods.

tour.title: WASM Attention & Mincut Family
tour.description: Building on the WASM cores, this family layers retrieval-quality features: ruvector-attention-wasm and the larger ruvector-attention-unified-wasm bundle attention scoring, ruvector-mincut-wasm and ruvector-mincut-gated-transformer-wasm offer mincut-based partitioning of candidate sets, and ruvector-hyperbolic-hnsw-wasm provides the curved-space HNSW variant. These crates compose with the cores from Step 2 to deliver advanced retrieval entirely in-browser.

tour.title: Node.js Bindings — Server-Side Bridge
tour.description: Where Steps 2-3 target the browser, this layer crosses into Node.js via napi-rs/neon. Each *-node crate (attention, gnn, graph, diskann, mincut) is a thin adapter exposing native-speed RuVector subsystems to server-side JS, while ruvector-attention-cli demonstrates the same primitives behind a standalone command-line. The pattern mirrors the WASM crates but trades portability for native performance.

tour.title: Specialized WASM — Domain Encoders
tour.description: These crates package domain-specific encoders and compression techniques: ruvector-gnn-wasm runs graph neural nets in-browser, ruvector-rabitq-wasm implements RaBitQ binary quantization, ruvector-domain-expansion(-wasm) widens vectors with learned projections, ruvector-economy-wasm and ruvector-exotic-wasm provide alternate encoding schemes, and ruvector-sparsifier-wasm prunes dense embeddings. Each pairs a native crate (the algorithm) with a -wasm crate (the binding).

tour.title: Routing Stack — Core, CLI, FFI, WASM
tour.description: The router is RuVector's embeddable vector-routing engine, designed to drop into heterogeneous hosts. ruvector-router-core holds the index, distance kernels (euclidean/cosine/dot/manhattan), and error model; ruvector-router-cli wraps it for shell use; ruvector-router-ffi exposes a C ABI for non-Rust callers; ruvector-router-wasm publishes the same engine as a browser module. Notice how one core crate fans out to three transport-specific surfaces.

tour.title: Search Infrastructure — Native Engines
tour.description: Native, server-side search and supporting plumbing: ruvector-diskann is the on-disk ANN index, ruvector-hyperbolic-hnsw is its curved-space sibling, ruvector-server hosts them over HTTP, ruvector-bench runs reproducible benchmarks, and ruvector-profiler/ruvector-metrics expose observability hooks. ruvector-collections, ruvector-crv, ruvector-dither, and ruvector-filter supply the data structures and post-processing utilities that wrap around the indexes.

tour.title: Thermal & Profiling — Hardware-Aware Runtime
tour.description: The capstone layer makes RuVector hardware-conscious. ruos-thermal reads CPU temperatures, derives ClockProfiles, and recommends target frequencies so search workloads back off before thermal throttling; thermorust offers a lower-level temperature crate; the profiling utility provides a unified surface for the metrics emitted by Step 7's engines. Together they let operators close the loop between query load, silicon heat, and routing decisions made by the Step 6 router.

tour.title: Cluster Overview: 14 Crates, 5 Subsystems
tour.description: Slice 10d collects RuVector's specialized AI/ML extension crates into five tightly-themed layers: LLM extras (CLI + WASM + retrieval/diffusion + sparse attention), a binary decompiler, a sublinear solver, a temporal-tensor compression store, and a graph transformer. Each subsystem ships a native Rust core and most have Node.js (napi) and/or WASM language bindings, giving the same engines a triple deployment target: server, browser, and Node.

tour.title: LLM Extras: CLI, WASM, Retrieval-Diffusion, Sparse Attention
tour.description: The LLM layer surrounds RuVector's core inference with four companions. ruvllm-cli is the user-facing binary that dispatches into chat/serve/quantize/benchmark/download subcommands and centralizes model metadata in models.rs. ruvllm-wasm exposes IntelligentLLMWasm to browsers/Node; ruvllm_retrieval_diffusion implements a Retriever/Diffuser pair for RAG-style sampling; ruvllm_sparse_attention provides a Tensor3 primitive and an F32Ext math trait that the sparse kernels build on. Together they form the 'LLM application surface' on top of the engine.

tour.title: Decompiler: Binary IR to Reconstructed Code
tour.description: ruvector-decompiler reverses compiled binaries back into structured IR. lib.rs declares the public module surface; types.rs (the cluster's #2 fan-in node at 13 incoming edges) defines the core IR data structures shared everywhere; inferrer.rs runs the type/shape inference passes, graph.rs holds the call/control-flow graph, training.rs handles the ML-assisted reconstruction model, and ruvector-decompiler-wasm exposes the engine to JS sandboxes for in-browser binary analysis.

tour.title: Solver: Sublinear Constraint Engine + Bindings
tour.description: ruvector-solver is the most depended-upon crate in the slice. types.rs (fan-in 25 — the single most-imported file) defines CsrMatrix sparse storage and the Algorithm enum used everywhere; error.rs (fan-in 11) and traits.rs (fan-in 9, three core traits) lock down the contract every solver backend implements. The solver ships through two binding crates: ruvector-solver-node wraps it as a napi NapiSolver for Node.js, while ruvector-solver-wasm exposes JsSolver and an analyze_sparsity helper to browsers.

tour.title: Temporal Tensor: Quantized, Delta-Encoded Tiered Storage
tour.description: ruvector-temporal-tensor is a purpose-built storage stack for time-varying tensor data. The pipeline flows bitpack -> quantizer (per-group scaled integer with variable bit-width) -> delta (sparse delta chains across time) -> segment (self-describing binary format) -> compressor (high-level facade) -> store (TieredStore with BlockKey/Tier/BlockIO) -> tiering (exponential-decay scoring and cold-tier migration). The lib.rs crate root re-exports all seven modules so callers see a single flat API.

tour.title: Graph Transformer Core: Five Attention Paradigms in One Engine
tour.description: ruvector-graph-transformer composes five distinct attention/message-passing paradigms behind one GraphTransformer entry point in lib.rs. sublinear_attention.rs uses LSH+PPR sampling to escape O(n^2); physics.rs adds Hamiltonian, gauge-equivariant, Lagrangian, and conservative-PDE attentions; manifold.rs operates on product Riemannian manifolds with curvature-adaptive routing and a Riemannian Adam optimizer; biological.rs implements spiking/dendritic/Hebbian/STDP primitives; verified_training.rs gates every training step on invariants with rollback strategies. config.rs and error.rs (fan-in 9 and 10) bind the subsystems with shared configuration and a unified error enum.

tour.title: Graph Transformer Bindings: Node + WASM Deployment
tour.description: The graph transformer ships to non-Rust runtimes through two thin binding crates. ruvector-graph-transformer-node wraps the engine as a napi GraphTransformer for Node.js servers, and ruvector-graph-transformer-wasm exposes a JsGraphTransformer to wasm-bindgen consumers (browser, edge workers, Deno). Both wrap the same underlying Rust GraphTransformer composition from Step 6 — the same composition of five attention paradigms — proving the slice's recurring 'one Rust core, three language targets' deployment shape.

tour.title: Cluster Overview — the 12 crates
tour.description: Slice 10e is the distributed storage cluster of RuVector. It groups twelve Rust crates into six layers: CRDT deltas, Raft replication, the RuLake/RAIRS storage tier, Tiny Dancer routing, the Verified+Acorn trust layer, and the Kalshi prediction-market integration. This first stop names every top-level crate so later steps slot into a known map.

tour.title: Delta family — CRDT primitives
tour.description: Every state change in the cluster is encoded as a delta. ruvector-delta-core defines the algebraic delta (compose, inverse, identity), while delta-consensus carries vector/Lamport clocks, delta-graph and delta-index apply deltas to graph and ANN structures, and delta-wasm exposes the same primitives to browser clients. Understanding deltas first is essential — replication, snapshot, and coherence all transport them.

tour.title: Replication and Raft consensus
tour.description: Deltas only become durable cluster state once Raft agrees on them. ruvector-raft implements leader election and log replication; ruvector-replication is the transport that ships committed deltas to followers; ruvector-snapshot compacts the log into restorable snapshots; ruvector-coherence enforces cross-replica invariants. Together they keep the cluster consistent under churn.

tour.title: Lake & RAIRS — long-term storage substrate
tour.description: Below the hot Raft path sits the analytical/archival tier. ruvector-rulake is the object-store-backed data lake (with a filesystem backend for tests and federation smoke-tests). ruvector-rairs layers retrieval and indexing on top of the lake — IVF clustering, k-means training, and the SEIL/RAIRS train pipelines convert raw lake contents into searchable vector indexes.

tour.title: Tiny Dancer — FastGRNN routing fabric
tour.description: Tiny Dancer decides where each request goes. The core crate trains a FastGRNN model (model.rs, training.rs) which the Router consults at runtime; admin-server.rs exposes the routing decisions and health/readiness over HTTP; optimization.rs quantizes weights to int8 for fast inference; circuit_breaker.rs trips the router away from unhealthy shards. This is the data-plane brain of the cluster.

tour.title: Verified & Acorn — gated proofs over fast indexes
tour.description: ruvector-verified turns each search/insert into an attested computation. FastTermArena is a pooled term store, the gated tier router (route_proof / verify_tiered) chooses cheap vs. strong proofs per request, and pipeline.rs composes verification stages. ruvector-acorn provides the filtered ANN engine that Verified gates — AcornIndex and FilteredIndex implement the actual k-NN search the cluster serves.

tour.title: Kalshi — prediction-market signal source
tour.description: ruvector-kalshi is the cluster's outbound integration to the Kalshi prediction market. auth.rs (Signer/SignedHeaders) does RSA-PSS request signing, rest.rs and ws.rs/ws_client.rs handle REST and websocket streams, rate_limit.rs enforces per-route caps, normalize.rs reshapes Kalshi messages into internal events, and strategy_adapter.rs plus brain.rs (BrainClient/SharedMemory) bridge those events back into the cluster's decision logic. This is the final step because it sits on top of every layer below it.

tour.title: Quantum + HW accelerator cluster: workspace overview
tour.description: Slice 10c bundles RuVector's quantum simulation stack with three hardware-accelerator paths (Hailo NPU, FPGA transformer, mmWave radar) and the sparse-inference engine that ties them to model serving. Start at the per-crate READMEs to anchor vocabulary across ruqu-core (state-vector sim + decoders), ruqu-algorithms (Grover/QAOA/VQE), ruqu-exotic (interference/swarm), the Hailo cluster coordinator, the FPGA transformer backends, and the sparse inference engine that feeds them.

tour.title: Quantum Core: ruqu-core simulator, gates, decoders, providers
tour.description: ruqu-core is the foundation: a pure-Rust state-vector simulator with Clifford+T support, surface-code decoders (UnionFind, sub-polynomial, hierarchical-tiled), Kraus-based noise models, transpilation, and a HardwareProvider abstraction that lets the same circuit target a local sim, IBM Quantum, or IonQ. The Simulator/QuantumState pair holds the live wavefunction while SurfaceCodeDecoder + decomposition::stoer_wagner_mincut drive error correction. Everything downstream in this slice consumes the Gate/QuantumCircuit/Hamiltonian types declared here.

tour.title: Quantum Algorithms + ruQu adaptive fabric
tour.description: Building on ruqu-core's primitives, ruqu-algorithms ships the canonical quantum recipes (Grover search with optimal iteration count, QAOA MaxCut, VQE hardware-efficient ansatz, and a surface-code QEC harness). ruQu wraps them in a 'classical nervous system' for live quantum hardware: a QuantumFabric/PatchGraph that streams syndromes through MWPMDecoder/StreamingDecoder, with AdaptiveThresholds + DriftDetector retuning the pipeline as device noise wanders.

tour.title: Exotic quantum-inspired reasoning + WASM bindings
tour.description: ruqu-exotic explores speculative reasoning kernels (interference, collapse, decay, swarm, reversible memory) used as discovery primitives, with cross-pipeline tests that combine decoherence, swarm reasoning, and QEC. ruqu-wasm then exports the deterministic chunks of ruqu-core/algorithms to the browser via wasm-bindgen, exposing WasmQuantumCircuit, Grover, and a QAOA-MaxCut entry point so JS callers can run small circuits client-side.

tour.title: Hailo NPU: single-device embedder up through the multi-Pi cluster
tour.description: The Hailo path layers cleanly: hailort-sys provides bindgen FFI to libhailort behind a `hailo` feature gate; ruvector-hailo's HailoEmbedder auto-selects between the native HEF pipeline (HefBackend) and a CPU fallback. ruvector-hailo-cluster turns that into a fleet: HailoClusterEmbedder orchestrates Discovery (Static/File/Tailscale), routes through a P2cPool (power-of-two-choices over an EmbeddingTransport), and quorum-checks model fingerprints across workers before serving embeddings.

tour.title: Sparse Inference: precision lanes, predictor, GGUF, model runners
tour.description: The sparse-inference crate is where models actually run. PrecisionLane enumerates 3/5/7-bit + FP lanes (with HardwareTarget gating SIMD/NPU/CPU choice), the LowRankPredictor forecasts which FFN neurons activate so SparseInferenceEngine can skip the rest, GgufParser loads quantized weights from disk, and three concrete ModelRunner impls (LlamaModel, LFM2Model, BertModel) plug into the unified Backend trait (CPU/NPU/WASM). SparseEmbeddingProvider wires the whole stack into RuVector's EmbeddingProvider interface.

tour.title: FPGA Transformer: artifacts, backends, FFI
tour.description: ruvector-fpga-transformer packages a transformer as a signed ModelArtifact (manifest + weights + test vectors, Ed25519-verified) and runs it through one of four interchangeable TransformerBackends: FpgaDaemonBackend (out-of-process over a socket), FpgaPcieBackend (direct DMA ring buffer + slot tracking), NativeSimBackend (software for CI), and WasmSimBackend. The top-level Engine binds backend + DefaultCoherenceGate + witness log, and the FFI module exposes both a C ABI (FpgaEngine/FpgaResult) and a wasm-bindgen surface for native and browser callers.

tour.title: mmWave Radar: frame parser + cluster bridge
tour.description: Finishing the slice, the mmwave crate is a streaming parser for Seeed MR60BHA1/MR60FDA1 radar frames that decodes presence, heart, and breath signals. The Hailo cluster ships a dedicated mmwave-bridge binary that turns those parsed radar features into embedding requests against the cluster from Step 5, closing the loop from sensor to NPU-served embedding. Integration tests cover both plain and TLS bridge flows.
